final.base_angle: narrative (THE KEEPING). Tie-break: the judges' overall scores tie 16-16 (KEEPING 9+7, HEADLIGHTS 8+8, BEHELD 7+6). THE KEEPING wins the three criteria the client wrote down. First, its escape logic is deduced from environmental clues. Second, it has one memorable ending with a final sting. Third, it keeps the fixed beats exactly and gives each a second meaning: his bell, his rope, his stopped stroke, his hand turning her face to yours. Its weaknesses are content weight, which can be cut. HEADLIGHTS' weaknesses are structural and cannot be grafted away: a note that dictates the solution, a twist on an optional page, and a back-seat-mirror trope. So the design takes THE KEEPING's story and rules, HEADLIGHTS' production discipline and BEHELD's AI engineering. Synthesizer fixes on top of the judges' lists: (1) The bathroom is cut entirely. Her upstairs anchor is her own nailed door, which she cannot pass ('She can't get past nails'). That motivates the B08 bell lure and keeps the dress out of her reach. (2) One rope mechanism, obeyed everywhere: a counterweight shuts the door, an iron drop-bolt locks it, and only a pull from the parlor lifts it. (3) Finale order: the parlor door stays shut while the bell rings; after the locket look the hall goes silent, the bell stops, she knocks, and Harlan opens a crack to check. (4) Locket rule: a lit, open locket within 4 m in her sight cone outranks your face, so raising it works even mid-chase. You hold it in front of your own face, and depth of field keeps her soft. (5) The bell lure weakens with each pull ('she learns'), with a 40 s floor, reset on death. (6) Harlan's bedroom gets a second door, creating a line-of-sight loop. (7) The under-stair closet opens off the back passage, so it only exists in the finale. (8) The guest-book line waiting for your name reads HARLAN in the sting. (9) 9 walkable spaces + 1 reused car set.
grafted: [HEADLIGHTS] Client beat 1 made airtight. GAS is painted out on Harlan's old sign; a hand-lettered ROOMS board with a tin VACANCY plate hangs under the lantern. One subtitle thought at the dead car: 'Forty-eight miles to anything. They'll have to put me up for the night.' The lure now baits lodgers, which is his trap.

[HEADLIGHTS] Production discipline: every space, prop, animation and sound is tagged M1/M2/M3, and layout and script freeze at M2 exit. M1 exit test: first-time strangers can name 'drip = near', 'drip stops = listening' and 'crack and hand to head = she sees' after one play, at 60 fps on an integrated GPU.

[HEADLIGHTS] Facade-only exterior: only the front wall and porch are detailed; the sides and back dissolve into rain and fog. The sedan is reused for 5-6 instanced wrecks and re-trimmed for the sting traveler.

[HEADLIGHTS, trimmed per the buildability judge] Lighting pipeline first, in M1 week 1: Blender-Python auto-UV2, lightmap bake, KTX2 export. Night + lightning lightmap blends only in U1-U3 at High; an exposure/light-probe pulse elsewhere and on Medium. Pre-warm shaders before the first flash and the first chase.
[HEADLIGHTS] Harlan's non-interactive appearances are static poses revealed by successive lightning flashes: the car push, the look-up, the foot of the stairs.
[HEADLIGHTS] A procedural single-stroke handwriting font with ink wobble, for the ledger, letter, guest book, chalked plates and the wet 'HARLAN'.

[HEADLIGHTS] Cross-floor drip tell: water beads and drips from the ceiling under wherever she stands. Used in the kitchen (B10) and through the stair treads onto your gloves in the under-stair closet (B11).
[HEADLIGHTS] Accessibility: optional captions/icons for every tell, and a reduced-flash mode (~150 ms fade-in, lower peak).
[HEADLIGHTS] Lightning never counts as 'lit' for her sight. The storm is purely the player's ally (thunder cover); the flash is only a scare and a vista.

[BEHELD, with the buildability caveat] Stop-motion: her pose is sampled at 8-12 fps with random held/dropped frames, while root motion and the camera run at full rate. A week-1 prototype compares skeleton-only against whole-pose (hair + gown) quantization before committing.

[BEHELD, conflict resolved] The head flopping upside down appears only when she bends to look under Harlan's iron bed during SEARCH. It is staged side-on, in silhouette, seen from the wardrobe across the room, and never face-on at slats (the buildability judge's face-exposure objection).

[BEHELD] AI engineering: an authored node graph with scripted door and stair traversal (no navmesh). Hearing attenuates on the room graph (closed door x0.5, floor x0.4, open stairwell exempt) with no raycasts. Explicit state priority. A testable hide rule: safe unless she had sight of you within 2 s of entry, or you are audible within 2 m.
[BEHELD] Post-death grace: she restarts at the anchor farthest from you, PATROL-only, with hearing -30% for 20 s. Key items can't be lost; the bell lure resets.
[BEHELD] Escalation tied to story turns: after her door is pried, and again after she finds the cut hem, her listening stops shorten and she LOOKs more often.
[BEHELD] Post-sprint panting is audible at ~2.5 m for 4 s, even inside a hide, with no meter UI. It teaches 'break line of sight early'.

[BEHELD + buildability judge] Guaranteed ways to break line of sight: Harlan's bedroom gets a second hallway door (the old dressing-room door), and the servants' stair is an always-safe reset she never uses.
[Buildability judge] Production caps: every document 60 words or fewer with one key line; every lit character shot held under 3 s; tell sounds prototyped in M1 before art polish.
[Horror-craft judge] Harlan's nonstop B10 bell is framed as the same rule turned against you. You are now on the parlor's floor, and the drip comes down the main stair toward you.
cut: Bathroom cut entirely, further than the judge's closed-door version. Her upstairs anchor becomes her own boarded door. The tub, the soaking apron and the tub exit beat go too; the mask-making kit moves to Harlan's bedroom.
Separate pickup dashboard for the sting: replaced by the sedan interior re-trimmed (maroon, air freshener, blinking fuel lamp).
Daylight walk through the dead-car field: replaced by ~30 s of blue-hour mist. Your car sits at the NEAR end of the row, and the wrecks stay silhouettes, never lit by day.
Harlan's continuous animations (car push, bell-ringing glimpse, the fall): replaced by static lightning poses, audio only, and a pre-rendered wall-shadow clip. The opening is his only authored clip.
Dust-sheet pulls, by her and by the player: the sheet has already slid off the dress's shoulder, and her hand goes straight to the cut hem.
The unexplained 'parlor door opens for her': she now knocks, and Harlan, hearing silence and then a knock, opens a crack to check.
The immediate 'raise the locket' prompt: shown once, only after the first failed finale approach.
Jerry can held in hand: now a silent inventory item with no hand model, so the finale's hands hold only the flashlight and the locket.

Readables cut: the 1976 calendar, the forty dollars and both snapshots (the hall portrait now carries the dress). What remains is the guest book, 3 ledger pages and the letter, each 60 words or fewer.
Treadle machine as a hero prop: now a dust-sheeted shape. The letter sits in the sewing basket with the shears.
Porch swing and the pantry hide: cut. The kitchen is hideless by design; the servants' stair is its escape route.
Live rear-view reflection: replaced by a pre-rendered mirror plate.
Lightning lightmap variants everywhere: kept only in U1-U3 at High; an exposure/probe pulse elsewhere.
DO NOT IMPORT: the back-seat rear-view-mirror sting. It is a trope and weaker than the mirrored parlor tableau.
DO NOT IMPORT: a player-performed beheading or hood-view stroke. Ada ends Harlan, and gore stays off the player's hands.
DO NOT IMPORT: throwable bottles, the chatelaine jingle, the cupped beam, a breath/stamina meter UI.
DO NOT IMPORT: any rules card or note that spells out the solution. The ceiling is 'If she ever sees it she'll know me.'
DO NOT IMPORT: a cellar/bulkhead, or the man refuelling your car offscreen. The kitchen can row with your chalked plate is the fuel clue.
DO NOT IMPORT: synthesized voices (the chase shriek). Her near-sob is breath and water, not a voice.
No cube-shadowed lights in play. The flashlight is the only shadow caster; the parlor candle casts shadows only in parlor cutscenes, with a silhouette-gobo fallback.

design.title: THE KEEPING
design.logline: Out of gas on a county road in the rain, you ring the bell of the only lit house for miles, under a lantern-lit sign that says ROOMS. The door opens by itself. In the first room on the right a man in a feed-sack mask is beheading a woman, and both of them turn to look at you. She hunts you through the house until you work out whose face she has really been looking for.
design.lore:
SETTING. County Road 9, emptied by the interstate. Tuesday 11 October 1994: no phone, a cassette deck, a fuel needle below E.

THE HOUSE. Stroud's Gas & Feed served the road until its pump ran dry in the early seventies. Harlan Stroud married Ada Lind, a seamstress from Carvel, in 1968. By 1976 the marriage was locks, bruises and a bell: when Harlan rang, Ada came. She saved sewing money in a biscuit tin, wrote to her sister Ruth, and bought a seat on the 6:10 bus for Tuesday 12 October. Harlan found the tin. On the night of the 11th he held her under in the rain cistern beneath the kitchen floor (the well) and padlocked the hatch. He told Carvel she had run off. Nobody looked for her, mourned her or buried her.

WHAT SHE IS. Whatever the water keeps comes back up. Three nights later Ada climbed out: a revenant, one of the unmourned drowned, who wants one thing, the face of the man who held her under. The water clouded her eyes, so she must bring her face close to a face to know it. Any face that is not his she drags down into the well, and each stranger buys weeks of quiet. She cannot get past iron nails. She still comes to the bell. She remembers her room and her dress. And she learns.

WHAT HE IS. Nothing supernatural: a man who murdered his wife and made himself her jailer. His mother's receipt book said to take the head and give it back to the water. That holds her one night; about six thousand pencil tallies on the parlor wall count those nights. He hides the only way that works: a feed sack over his head, crepe over every mirror, his face knifed out of every photograph. The locket he gave her, the one image he could not destroy, he believes went down the well with her. In 1977 a drifter kept her quiet a month, and Harlan learned he could buy rest. He painted out the GAS on his sign and hung a ROOMS board, lit with gasoline siphoned from the last guest's car. He wired every bell to ring in the parlor, hung the front door on a rope and nailed every sash. His guest book holds eleven names; nine cars rust in the east field. She has to take them herself: one he killed himself didn't hold her an hour. He tells his ledger he does it so she can't walk the road. That is also true.

THE ROPE (one mechanism, obeyed everywhere). A counterweight pulls the front door shut. An iron drop-bolt, boxed out of reach above the transom, locks it. One rope runs from the bolt over three cornice pulleys to a cleat in the parlor. A pull lifts the bolt and draws the door open. Cleated, it stays open. Released, the weight slams it and the bolt drops. Only a hand in the parlor can open it.

THE TWIST. Nothing in the opening was chance. The ROOMS lantern was bait. The bell you rang was his signal, and the door that opened by itself was his rope. The beheading was his nightly chore, eighteen years to the night, and he stopped the second stroke on purpose. Both of them looked at you because he turned her face to the doorway by the hair so she would see yours. Then he let the rope go, and the slam and the stairs herded you upward like the eleven before you. She was never hunting you. She is hunting him, and she can't see him.

THE WAY OUT. The last image of his face is in the locket, sewn into the hem of her wedding dress beside her bus ticket in a room nailed shut since 1976. Hold his face up in your light and let her look.

THE STING. She takes him, pulls his rope and lets you go. But she learns: whoever holds the rope keeps the house.

characters.name: The Traveler
characters.role: Player character: first person, silent, unnamed, driving County Road 9 on 11 October 1994.
characters.appearance: Never seen. The player only sees leather driving gloves, a rain-dark coat sleeve and a steel two-cell flashlight. A tired late-80s sedan, plate RVX-318, is shown clearly in the opening because it pays off on a chalked can and in the field.
characters.behavior: No voice. One subtitle thought in the opening: 'Forty-eight miles to anything. They'll have to put me up for the night.' Camera and hands carry the emotion: the lock-up at the threshold, the beam trembling when she is near, held breath and heartbeat in hides, panting after sprints.

characters.name: Ada Stroud (the woman)
characters.role: The single AI chaser: a revenant, one of the unmourned drowned, and the story's true victim.
characters.appearance: Slight and barefoot, in a sodden ivory nightgown stained grey-green with cistern silt. Grey-blue skin shows only at the hands and feet. Very long black hair is plastered wet over her whole face; one clouded, iris-less white eye is the most ever shown. She drips constantly. After the opening her neck is half-severed: the head hangs or lolls on a spring joint unless she lifts it in her hand. A pale line on her throat marks where a locket chain sat. She is seen in darkness, silhouette or through slats, and never lit for more than 3 s.
characters.behavior:
Stop-motion stutter: her pose is sampled at 8-12 fps while she moves smoothly through space.
- Head hanging means she is blind; she hunts by sound and by the warmth of light.
- To see, she lifts her head in her hand with a bone crack, the key tell.
- She opens ordinary doors, slowly, but can't get past nails. Between hunts she stands at her own boarded door, forehead to the planks, scraping at the nail heads.
- She always goes to a ringing bell; in life, when he rang, she came.
- She goes close to every face she finds.
- She is human at the dress.
- She learns.

characters.name: Harlan Stroud (the man)
characters.role: Scripted presence only, never a chaser: husband, murderer, jailer and trapper.
characters.appearance: Big, stooped, sixties. Burlap feed sack over his head (faded STROUD FEED & SEED stencil, uneven eyeholes, twine at the neck), flannel, suspenders, black rubber apron, rubber boots, gloves, hog cleaver. His face is never rendered; his unmasking is the shadow of a bare head on a wall.
characters.behavior:
Slow; never runs, never attacks ('She has to take them herself'). His rocking chair creaks up through the floors like a metronome and stops when he moves. Appearances:
- the opening tableau, his only authored clip
- three static lightning poses: pushing your car, looking up at your window, watching from the foot of the stairs
- rocking under the floor grate, tilting the sack up at you
- the sack in the parlor door gap, then a pre-rendered shadow
- his head in a sack in the sting

His bell is heard, never seen. He watches every guest be taken.

characters.name: The next traveler
characters.role: Point of view for the final sting only.
characters.appearance: Unseen: the same sedan interior re-trimmed (maroon, pine air freshener, fuel lamp blinking).
characters.behavior: Knocks, rings the bell and freezes on the threshold: the player's opening, shot for shot.

house_layout.name: County Road 9 & the ROOMS sign

house_layout.description:
Where the car dies at the gate, where you leave, and where the sting begins.
- A roadside post carries the old STROUD'S GAS & FEED sign with GAS painted out. Under it hang a hand-lettered ROOMS board and a tin VACANCY plate that creaks in the wind, lit by a lantern in a tin box.
- A STROUD mailbox and a fence line with reflector posts.
- A NEXT SERVICES 48 MI card further back, seen only in C1.

Mostly seen from the car; the player walks only from the car to the gate.

player's sedan RVX-318 at the gate (until B07)

house_layout.name: Drive, yard, porch & east field
house_layout.size_m: drive about 25 x 5 m; porch 9 x 2.5 m; facade 11 m wide; east-field vista about 60 x 30 m (lightning and mist only)
house_layout.description:
Only the front facade and porch are built in detail; the sides and back dissolve into rain and fog.
- The gravel drive passes a dead 1950s pump (dry nozzle, price dial frozen at 1976, STROUD'S GAS & FEED), so there is no gas here.
- Every sash on the porch is nailed and shuttered.
- Right of the door, candlelight leaks through the parlor shutters, where a shadow rises and falls to the rasp of a whetstone.
- The front door has an iron knocker, a fanlight and a brass bell-pull knob wired to the parlor.
- East of the drive, nine dead cars sit in the weeds: a lightning vista from upstairs, grey shapes in the blue-hour mist. Your car ends up at the near end of the row.

key_contents: front door: knocker, fanlight, bell-pull knob
nailed, shuttered windows; lit parlor shutters
row of 9 wrecks (5-6 instanced sedan variants), plus your car after B07

house_layout.name: Entrance hall & main stair
house_layout.size_m: 3.6 x 9 m, ceiling 3.2 m; stair 1.1 m wide, 16 risers rising north along the west wall
house_layout.description:
Side-hall plan. The front door is at the south end.
- The parlor door is on the right (east), immediately inside: the first room on the right.
- The stair rises along the left wall.
- A hall table holds a candle (its flame leans toward her) and the open guest book.
- A tall mirror is covered in crepe.
- The wedding portrait shows the bride veiled, in the dress you'll find upstairs, with the groom's face knifed out.
- The door rope runs on three pulleys along the east cornice from the bolt box into the parlor, beside the bell wire.
- At the north end, the back passage leads to the kitchen (bolted from the kitchen side until B10). The under-stair closet opens off that passage.

This is the stage for the opening and the finale.

G2: parlor door (locked after the opening; threshold view only)
G3: back passage (bolted from the kitchen side until B10), with the under-stair closet off it

rope, 3 pulleys, bolt box, bell wire

house_layout.name: The parlor, the first room on the right
house_layout.description:
Harlan's room and the house's altar, dressed for three fixed camera views and never free-roamed.
- A sawbuck table under a rubber sheet, with a zinc bucket.
- His rocking chair, facing the door.
- The north wall (shared with the kitchen) is covered to the picture rail in pencil tallies.
- A spring bell above the door, wired to every pull.
- The rope cleat.
- A candle on the near end of the table throws the figures' shadows across the tally wall; another stands on the mantel under a crepe mirror.
- The hog cleaver.

Seen from the threshold (opening, finale, sting) and through the bedroom's floor grate.

house_layout.name: Kitchen & back passage
house_layout.size_m: 5 x 5.5 m, plus a 1.2 x 3 m back passage
house_layout.description:
Cold iron stove, pump sink, table.
- The cistern hatch (the well) is padlocked on the OUTSIDE, its edges splintered upward from beneath. Water seeps between the boards, and something thumps once against the lid.
- Twelve jerry cans are chalked with licence plates: eleven full of the dead guests' gasoline, one fresh and empty, chalked RVX-318.
- The back door is bricked.
- The servants' stair arrives in the north-east corner; the back passage runs west to the hall, bolted on this side.
- Water beads and drips from the ceiling when she crosses above.

No hide here, by design.
connections: G1: back passage (bolt on the kitchen side)

house_layout.name: Upper hallway & landing
house_layout.size_m: 2 x 9 m, ceiling 2.9 m; balustrade open to the stairwell on the west
house_layout.description:
The stair arrives at the north end, and the hallway doubles back south along the balustrade, so you can see her climbing below. A runner rug is quiet; the bare-board margins are louder. Two marked creakers lie between the armoire and Ada's door.

East wall, north to south:
- Ada's door beside the stair top, boarded with three planks (her vigil spot)
- 5 m on, the armoire (first hide)
- 1.5 m on, Harlan's bedroom door
- near the south end, his dressing-room door

The south window is the main lightning source. The 1970 photo of the couple at the pump has his face knifed out.

U3: Ada's boarded door (passable after B08)

house_layout.name: Harlan's bedroom
house_layout.description:
Above the parlor, with two doors to the hall.
- Iron bed; nightstand with his farm-ledger diary and a low kerosene lamp (stand close and you are lit).
- An embroidered bell pull whose wire runs along the cornice toward the stair.
- A wardrobe (hide) packed with strangers' coats, a handbag and a trucker cap.
- A chair of spare sacks, twine and scissors.
- A crepe-covered washstand mirror.
- The nailed east window over the field, with a claw hammer and a can of square nails on the sill.
- A cast-iron floor register looking straight down into the parlor.

house_layout.name: Ada's sewing room
house_layout.description:
Boarded shut since 1976.
- Dust sheets over a chair, a trunk and a treadle-machine shape.
- Her wedding dress on a dummy by the window. Its sheet has slid off one shoulder over eighteen years, and the hem is exposed.
- A sewing basket holds shears and an unsent letter.
- A heavy wardrobe (hide) against the north wall hides the servants' stair door; its back boards are loose and breathe cold air.
connections: U4: through the back of the wardrobe
key_contents: dress on dummy (intact and cut-hem states)
hem bundle: locket and bus ticket
wardrobe with loose back (hide and route)

house_layout.name: Servants' back stair
house_layout.size_m: 0.8 m wide, 14 steep risers with one winder; about 1 x 3.5 m
house_layout.description: Enclosed, pitch black and curtained with cobwebs, with one tight turn; the well's slosh grows louder as you descend. It is the only way down that avoids the hall, and she never uses it: the one always-safe route.

beats.title: Empty
beats.location: Car interior to County Road 9, at the gate
beats.description: Opening cutscene C1 (about 55 s, in-engine, first person). Night, hard rain, fog. Wipers, radio static, the needle under E, the low-fuel chime. NEXT SERVICES 48 MI slides past. Out of the dark comes an old STROUD'S GAS & FEED sign with GAS painted out; a hand-lettered ROOMS board and a tin VACANCY plate creak under a lantern. The engine coughs and dies, and the car rolls to a stop at the gate. Lightning shows a peeling clapboard house on a rise: nailed shutters, a dead pump, one window right of the door leaking candlelight. Subtitle: 'Forty-eight miles to anything. They'll have to put me up for the night.' The camera rises past the taillights on plate RVX-318 as you step into the rain. No phone, no other light for miles: the only choice is to ask to stay the night. Tension 2 to 4.
beats.player_goal: Watch; step out and go to the house.
beats.setpiece: The car dies under the lantern-lit ROOMS sign; lightning reveals the house.

beats.title: Stroud's
beats.description: First control; the flashlight (F) is needed at once. Walk up the drive past the dead pump (dial frozen at 1976 prices): no gas here either. Nail heads glint in every sash. Through the parlor shutters to the right of the door, a shadow rises and falls to the rasp of a whetstone. Knock: nothing, and the rasp goes on. Pull the bell knob: a bell rings inside, off to the RIGHT, and the rasp stops. A long beat. Inside, overhead, a rope runs through pulleys, the latch clacks, and the front door swings open by itself onto a dark hall. Without text, this teaches that the doorbell rings in the parlor and that the door is worked from in there. Tension 4 to 6.
beats.player_goal: Find someone who will let you stay: knock, then ring the bell.
beats.setpiece: The door that opens by itself.

beats.title: The First Room on the Right
beats.location: Entrance hall to the parlor threshold
beats.description:
Inside: a candle beside the open guest book (optional read: eleven names ruled through, tonight's date with the name blank). A crepe-covered mirror, and a wedding portrait with the groom's face knifed out. Look up and you see the rope running from a bolt box above the door into the parlor. The first door on the right stands ajar and candlelit, and from it comes one wet chop.

At the threshold the controls lock and the player freezes (C2, about 30 s). A candle on the near end of a long table throws the scene huge across a far wall covered in pencil tallies. A man in a feed-sack mask and rubber apron stands over a woman bent face-down across the table on a rubber sheet; spatter glistens, and her wet black hair hangs to the floor. His second stroke is raised, and stops. He takes a fistful of her hair and turns her face to the doorway. One clouded eye opens behind the hair. The sack's eyeholes turn to you. Both of them look at you for three heartbeats.

He lets the rope slip from its cleat. It runs over your head, and behind you the front door slams and the bolt drops. She slides off the table and rises, her head lolling on the half-cut neck; behind her the parlor door swings shut and a key turns. Control returns mid-lurch. Tension 6 to 10.
beats.player_goal: Frozen at first; then run.
beats.setpiece: The beheading as shadow-play on the tally wall; the double look; the door slam.

beats.title: Up
beats.description: Scripted chase with a guaranteed near-miss: she is held 2-4 m behind and catches you only if you stand still for more than 2 s. The front door won't budge, the parlor is shut, and the far end of the hall is a dead end (its passage door is bolted from the other side). Lightning shows the stair as the only way. She follows in stuttering bursts, one hand on the banister, head swinging. At the top the hallway doubles back along the balustrade, so you see her climbing through the balusters. A flash through the south window picks out an armoire standing ajar. Tension 10.
beats.player_goal: Get away from her and hide.
beats.setpiece: Chase up the stairs with her visible through the balusters.

beats.title: Hold Your Breath
beats.location: Upper hallway: the armoire, then her vigil
beats.description: The first hide is taught by demonstration and cannot be failed. Through the slats you hear wet slaps on the stairs and the drip. At the top she stops, and the drip stops too: she is listening. She comes down the runner and stands at the slats. A gurgle; a crack of bone as her hand lifts her head; in a lightning flash the hair parts on one white eye. Prompt: hold breath (Space). She lowers her head, the drip resumes, and she drifts back to the door beside the stair top, boarded with three planks. She stands with her forehead against it, scraping at the nail heads. Now sneak out. She is about 5 m away, blind and listening: walking on the runner (2 m radius) or crouching (1.5 m) is safe, running (10 m) is not. Slip 1.5 m south into Harlan's bedroom. Checkpoint; the vertical slice ends here. Tension 10 to 5.
beats.player_goal: Stay hidden while she looks; then sneak away from her vigil.
beats.setpiece: The eye at the slats; the woman scraping at her own nailed door.

beats.title: His Room
beats.location: Harlan's bedroom and the upper hallway
beats.description:
A stealth loop you can read. She cycles from her door to the stair top (LOOK), down the runner, glances through Harlan's two doorways, stops at the south window (LOOK), and goes back. Her footprints glisten in the beam and dry out, and the drip gives her away through walls. Once, a thunder roll audibly swallows her footsteps.

Harlan's bedroom sits over the parlor, and its two doors make a loop. The room holds:
- the ledger (three short pages) beside a low lamp
- an embroidered bell pull whose wire runs toward the stair
- a wardrobe of strangers' coats (hide)
- a chair of spare sacks and twine where he makes his faces
- a crepe-covered mirror
- on the nailed window's sill, a claw hammer and a can of square nails
- a floor register looking straight down into the parlor: the tally wall, the table, and the rocking chair, empty but still rocking

Tension 5 to 6.
beats.player_goal: Look for a way out; read the ledger; take the hammer.
beats.setpiece: The floor-grate view down into the parlor.

beats.title: He Looks Up
beats.description:
Lifting the hammer triggers C3; you keep look control.
- Flash: nine dead cars in the weeds.
- Flash: the man in the sack pushing YOUR car (RVX-318) off the drive to join them.
- Flash: he has stopped and lifted his head to your window.
- Darkness.
- Flash: gone.

Below, the front door slams and the bolt drops, and the rocking resumes under your feet. The grate now shows him in the chair with the cleaver across his knees; if you peek, the sack tilts up at you. No help is coming; you are the next car. Tension 6 to 8 to 6.
beats.player_goal: Understand there is no help and no car.
beats.setpiece: The field of cars and the man who looks up.

beats.title: Nailed Shut
beats.location: Upper hallway: Ada's door beside the stair top
beats.description: The one door you can't open is boarded, and it is the door she keeps standing at. Pull the bell by his bed: far below the parlor bell jangles, the drip recedes down the stairs, and through the grate you hear her scraping at the parlor door. The storm is at its peak, with a flash every 12 s or so. Pry each board inside a thunder roll: flash, count, rumble, pull. A pry outside the rumble is a 14 m screech that carries down the stairwell and brings her back. In one flash a figure stands at the foot of the stairs, sack tilted up, watching; in the next he is gone. If she returns, hide in the armoire. Boards you have pried stay pried. Each later pull holds her downstairs for less time (60, then 50, then 40 s): she learns. Tension 5 to 8.
beats.player_goal: Open Ada's door without bringing her back.
beats.setpiece: Prying in the thunder; the watcher at the foot of the stairs.

beats.title: The Hem
beats.description:
Untouched since 1976. Dust sheets over a chair, a trunk and a treadle-machine shape. By the window stands the wedding dress from the hall portrait, its sheet slid off one shoulder and the hem exposed. In the sewing basket: shears and an unsent letter. Cut the hem (hold) and a bundle drops: a 6:10 bus ticket for 12 October 1976 and a locket engraved 'A. from H. 1968'. Inside is a water-bloomed photo. Most of the image is gone, but not a young man's eyes and jaw: the only face of Harlan left in the world.

The drip returns on the landing. Hide in her wardrobe (C4). Through the slats she goes to the dress, her hand finds the cut hem, and she makes a long wet sound that is almost a sob. Her head lifts toward you: hold your breath, and the boards at your back give a little. She leaves. The wardrobe's back breathes cold air; push through to the servants' stair. Tension 6 to 9 to 4.
beats.player_goal: Find what Harlan fears; survive her visit.
beats.setpiece: Ada and her wedding dress, seen from the hide.

beats.title: What the Water Keeps
beats.description: A narrow stair choked with cobwebs, with one turn; the slosh below grows louder. In the kitchen the well's hatch is padlocked on the OUTSIDE and splintered upward from beneath; water seeps up, and something thumps once against the lid. Water beads on the ceiling and drips as she crosses the floor above. A row of jerry cans is chalked with licence plates, full of the dead guests' gasoline, and at the end sits a fresh, empty can already chalked RVX-318. Take a full one: your tank is empty. It grates on the floor. Through the shared wall the rocking stops, and the parlor bell starts ringing and doesn't stop. All night the bell pulled her away from you; now you are on the parlor's floor, and the drip starts down the main stair toward you. Slide the back-passage bolt. Tension 6 to 8.
beats.player_goal: Learn the truth; take fuel; head for the front door.
beats.setpiece: The thump under the hatch; your plate on the empty can.

beats.title: Let Her Look
beats.location: Back passage, entrance hall, parlor threshold
beats.description:
She is coming down the stair. Duck into the under-stair closet and she passes over your head, dripping through the treads onto your gloves. The front door is still bolted by the rope. Everything says run. Instead: light on, raise the open locket into the beam in front of your face (RMB), and let her come. She stops at arm's length. The crack; her hand lifts her head; one eye. The locket is sharp in the beam, her face soft behind it. Her grey fingers close over it, and the chain slides from your glove. The hall goes silent, and a beat later the bell stops.

She knocks on the parlor door three times, slowly: your knock. The door opens a crack as he checks, showing candlelight and the sack's eyeholes. Her hand is in the gap before he can shut it. You are walked to the threshold, framed exactly as in the opening. He backs away, raising the cleaver by reflex; she walks into it; the candle dies. Lightning: her shadow pulls the sack from his head. Next flash: her shadow lifts his cleaver. Black. One stroke. The bell rings once. Then the rope zips through the pulleys overhead, and behind you the front door swings open onto grey mist. The parlor door closes. Tension 8 to 10 to 2.
beats.player_goal: Show her his face.
beats.setpiece: The locket look; the unmasking in shadow; the door that opens for you.

beats.title: Blue Hour
beats.location: Porch, drive, near end of the wreck row, road
beats.description: Release (C6, semi-interactive). The rain has stopped; the eaves drip; mist lies in the field with the wrecks as grey shapes. Your car sits at the near end of the row. Pour the can (hold) and turn the key: two coughs, then it catches, and the radio comes back mid-song. Roll past the pump; the ROOMS lantern gutters out as you pass. In the mirror the house sinks into the mist. Tension 2 to 1.
beats.player_goal: Leave.
beats.setpiece: The engine catches.

beats.title: The Keeping
beats.description: Sting C7, reusing the opening's camera paths. Weeks later, in the rain, a different dashboard with the fuel lamp blinking. The ROOMS lantern is lit again. A knock; the bell rings off to the right; the door opens by itself. In the guest book, the line that waited for your name reads HARLAN in wet, clumsy capitals, ruled through, with a blank line under it. From the opening's exact threshold and lens: candlelight, the tally wall with a fresh column of clumsy strokes, and Ada in his rocking chair with a round, heavy feed sack tied at the neck in her lap. The rocking stops. She lifts her own head in one hand; with the other she raises the sack by its knot and turns its eyeholes to the doorway, as he once turned hers. Both of them look at you. Black. One bell. THE KEEPING.
beats.player_goal: None. Watch.
beats.setpiece: The mirrored tableau.

states: SCRIPTED: cutscenes and set pieces. The opening rise; the B04 chase (held 2-4 m behind, catch only if you stand still for more than 2 s); the B05 slats look; the B09 dress visit.
VIGIL: anchor between hunts. Upstairs at her own boarded door (beside the dress after B09), forehead to the planks, scraping the nail heads for 15-30 s; blind, hearing normal.

PATROL: 0.9 m/s stutter-walk on an authored node loop, head hanging, with LOOK points at the stair top, the south window and the doorways. Upper loop: her door, stair top, runner, Harlan's two doors, south window. Ground loop (finale only): stair foot, parlor door, back passage, kitchen.
LISTEN: freezes about 1 s, head tilted toward a noise; the drip stops.
INVESTIGATE: walks at 1.4 m/s to a noise or light, then LOOKs.
LOOK: her hand lifts her head with a bone crack. 1.2 s wind-up (0.6 s if your beam touched her), 3 s of sight, then the head lowers.
CHASE: jerky 3.2 m/s bursts with her head held up in one hand. She follows running noise when sight breaks, and switches to SEARCH after 4 s with neither.
SEARCH: up to two LOOKs, nails dragged on plaster; in Harlan's room she looks under the bed (head flops upside down, side-on). Then 4-6 s listening at the nearest hide.
LURED: any bell, except during CHASE. She scrapes at the parlor door for 60 s, then 50, then 40 s (floor, reset on death), then climbs back up audibly.

FINALE: triggered whenever she sights the open, lit locket within 4 m, in LOOK, in CHASE or during the dress visit. She stops dead, comes to arm's length, looks, takes it, and carries it to the parlor door; C5 plays when you are in the hall.
CATCH: within 1 m in CHASE, bumping into her, or when she opens an occupied hide. Grab, then a 3 s death cutaway.
chaser_ai.senses:
SOUND (primary, always on). Every action has a noise radius at its source:
- crouch 1.5 m
- walk on the runner 2 m; walk on bare boards 4 m; the two marked creakers 7 m
- run 10 m, then post-sprint panting 2.5 m for 4 s
- door slow 3 m / fast 8 m
- pry 14 m
- gasp in a hide 3 m

Attenuation uses the authored room graph, not raycasts: each closed door x0.5, each floor x0.4, except through the open stairwell. During a thunder roll (2.5 s, starting about 1.5 s after each flash) she hears nothing.

LIGHT (always on; she feels it as warmth). A beam touching her body forces an instant fast LOOK toward it. A beam playing within 6 m of her draws her to INVESTIGATE. Fixed flames never lure her, but standing within 1.5 m of one makes you lit.

SIGHT (only while her head is lifted, during LOOK and CHASE). 60-degree cone: 14 m if you are lit, 5 m if you are dark, 2 m if you are dark and crouched. Lightning never counts as light. Being seen starts a CHASE; being seen entering a hide means that hide is found. The open, lit locket within 4 m outranks everything else she sees.
chaser_ai.rules:
1) No cheating: she knows where you are only through a sense event.
2) Head hanging means blind, always. She sees only in LOOK or CHASE, and only what is lit.
3) Priority: FINALE > CATCH > SCRIPTED > CHASE > LOOK > newest of LURED/INVESTIGATE > SEARCH > PATROL > VIGIL. She acts on the newest stimulus that reaches her. A bell reaches her anywhere in the house; a noise reaches her only within its attenuated radius. A bell never breaks a CHASE.
4) She opens ordinary doors, slowly and audibly. She cannot get past nails (her boarded door until it is pried, every nailed sash). She never opens the locked parlor door herself and never uses the servants' stair.
5) Hides (armoire, two wardrobes, under-stair closet) are safe unless she saw you within 2 s of entering or you are audible within 2 m. At the slats, hold your breath (Space, up to 7 s). A gasp makes her tear the door open.
6) To lose her: break line of sight, then stop running; after 4 s she SEARCHes.
7) Each successive bell pull holds her for less time (60/50/40 s, reset on death). She learns.
8) Thunder rolls mask all player sound.
9) Speeds: you walk 1.6, run 3.6 (no stamina, but you pant), crouch 0.9 m/s. She patrols at 0.9, investigates at 1.4, chases at 3.2. Straight lines gain ground but never lose her; corners, doors, Harlan's two-door loop and the servants' stair do.
10) Locket rule: whenever she is sighted and the open, lit locket is within 4 m in her cone, it outranks your face and she enters FINALE.
11) There is only one of her, never relocated where you can see; scripted moves happen behind doors or floors.
12) Harlan never attacks: he rings, watches and waits.
chaser_ai.tells:
- Drip: constant, spatialized, audible through walls; its rate follows her speed.
- Drip stops: she is listening; freeze.
- Bone crack and her hand rising to her jaw: she will see in 1.2 s.
- Throat gurgle: she is within about 5 m.
- Wet footprints glisten in the beam and dry over about 60 s.
- Candle and lamp flames lean toward her.
- Water beads on the ceiling under wherever she stands on the floor above.
- Nails on plaster: searching. Scraping at wood: at her vigil or lured to the parlor.
- Parlor bell: she is going downstairs.
- Head hanging: blind. Head held in her hand: she sees.
- A string cluster and heartbeat while she chases, falling silent when she loses you.
- Optional captions/icons for every tell.
chaser_ai.counterplay:
- Listen before you move. Walk the runner, crouch on bare boards, avoid the creakers.
- Flashlight off near her; never put the beam on her.
- When the drip stops, freeze. When you hear the crack, get out of her cone or into the dark.
- Break line of sight before hiding, and don't hide winded.
- Hold your breath at the slats.
- Do loud things (running, doors, prying) inside a thunder roll.
- Pull his bell to send her down, and spend the shrinking window well.
- Lose her through the bedroom's two doors or on the servants' stair.
- In the finale, reverse everything: light on, the open locket in the beam in front of your face, stand still, let her look.

obstacles_and_puzzles.name: Every Bell Rings in His Room (the lure)
obstacles_and_puzzles.where: Harlan's bedroom bell pull, sending her to the parlor door
obstacles_and_puzzles.solution: Pull the embroidered bell pull. The parlor bell rings, and she drops anything except a chase to go downstairs and scrape at the parlor door: 60 s, then 50, then 40 s (reset on death). Then she climbs back up, audibly. The upper floor is clear while she is down there.
obstacles_and_puzzles.clues: In B02 the doorbell rang off to the right, in the parlor, and the whetstone stopped. The bell wire runs from the pull along the cornice toward the stair. Ledger p3: 'She always comes to the bell.' On first use you hear the drip recede down the stairs and scraping through the floor grate.

obstacles_and_puzzles.name: Nailed Shut (pry in the thunder)
obstacles_and_puzzles.where: Ada's boarded door beside the stair top (her vigil spot)
obstacles_and_puzzles.solution: Take the hammer. Pry the three boards one at a time, each within a thunder roll (each pry is a 2 s hold). During this beat the storm flashes about every 12 s, so three rolls fit inside one bell window. A pry outside a roll is a 14 m screech that brings her back: hide, ring again, and continue. Pried boards stay pried. After 2 failures the rumbles last longer.
obstacles_and_puzzles.clues: Ledger p1: 'Nailed her room shut. She can't get past nails.' She keeps scraping at that door. Ledger p3: 'She can't hear a thing under thunder.' In B06 a roll swallowed her footsteps. The hammer sits beside a can of the same nails. The storm keeps a steady rhythm: flash, count, rumble.

obstacles_and_puzzles.name: The Hem
obstacles_and_puzzles.solution: Read the letter in the sewing basket. Cut the dress's hem with her shears and take the locket (and the ticket). Survive her visit in the wardrobe by holding your breath when her head lifts. Then push through the wardrobe's loose back to the servants' stair.
obstacles_and_puzzles.clues: Letter: 'the ticket's sewn in the hem of my wedding dress, with the locket.' The hall portrait shows her in that dress. Ledger p2: the picture 'went down the well with her'. That is why it matters, and why nobody looked. Ledger p1: 'I won't go in either.' In the wardrobe the boards give at your back, and cold air moans through them.

obstacles_and_puzzles.name: Let Her Look (the finale)
obstacles_and_puzzles.where: Entrance hall, between the under-stair closet and the parlor door
obstacles_and_puzzles.solution: Flashlight on. Raise the open locket (RMB) into the beam in front of your face and let her come. Whenever she has sight of the lit locket within 4 m (LOOK or a CHASE glance), she stops dead, looks and takes it. It works wherever she sees it, even in the dress scene; she then carries it down to his door, C5 plays when you are in the hall, and the drive waits on the fuel can. Running without it is not an instant fail: she chases, and the servants' stair lets you reset.
obstacles_and_puzzles.clues: Ledger p2: 'If she ever sees it she'll know me.' The sack, the crepe on every mirror and the knifed photos all say his face is the weapon. Every encounter has taught you that she sees only what is lit, and only with her head lifted. His nonstop bell tells you this is the moment. A one-time prompt appears only after the first failure.

design.escape_theorem:
GOAL: leave alive through the front door and drive away.

PREMISES (each clued in the house):
P1 EXIT: The front door is the only way out. [Every sash is nailed and shuttered, with the same nails on his sill; the kitchen door is bricked; the front door won't rattle open.]
P2 ROPE: The door opens only when the rope is pulled from the parlor. [B02: pulleys run and the door swings open. C2: the rope runs overhead and the door slams and bolts. The rope runs along the cornice into the parlor; the bolt box is out of reach.]
P3 KEEPER: The rope is Harlan's, and he means you for her; neither of them can be fought. [The opening; guest book: eleven names ruled through, tonight's blank; nine dead cars; your car pushed in among them; your plate chalked on an empty can.]
=> L1: You leave only if Harlan stops holding the rope, and only Ada can make him.
P4 HUNT: She hunts one face, his, and he survives by hiding it. [She lifts her head to every face; the sack; the crepe; the knifed photos; ledger: 'She can't find me if she can't see me.']
P5 RECOGNITION: If she sees his face, she will know him. [Ledger: 'If she ever sees it she'll know me, and that's the end of me.']
P6 FACE: One picture of his face survives in her locket, and it is not in the well: it is sewn into the hem of her wedding dress. [Ledger p2 against the letter.]
P7 SIGHT: She sees only while her head is lifted, and only what is lit. [Every encounter.]
=> L2: Put his face in your light where she will look (the open locket, held in the beam in front of your face) and let her come close.

ROUTE (linear; each step needs the one before):
1. Survive the chase; slip past her vigil into Harlan's bedroom.
2. Take the hammer; read the ledger; find the bell pull.
3. Pull the bell: she goes down to the parlor door for about 60 s.
4. Pry her three boards, one per thunder roll.
5. Read the letter; cut the hem: the locket.
6. Survive her visit in the wardrobe; go through its back and down the servants' stair to the kitchen.
7. Take a full can (your tank is empty).
8. Unbolt the back passage. In the hall, as his bell calls her onto you, raise the lit locket and let her look.

THEREFORE: she knows him, takes the locket and knocks at his door. Harlan opens a crack to check, and she takes him. She holds the rope now; she pulls it, and the front door opens. Can, tank, road.

COROLLARY (the sting): whoever holds the rope keeps the house, and she learns. [Ledger: 'She works the latches now. She learns.']
items: Flashlight: steel two-cell, always equipped (F). It lights your way. It lures her when it touches her or plays near her, and makes you visible when she looks. In the finale it must light the locket.
Car keys: carried from the opening; used at blue hour.
Claw hammer: from Harlan's sill; carried; pries Ada's three boards.
Sewing shears: used in place to cut the hem; not carried.
Ada's locket: key item. Engraved 'A. from H. 1968'; water-bloomed photo in which only young Harlan's eyes and jaw survive. RMB raises it, open, into the beam in front of your face.
Bus ticket: 'CARVEL 6:10, TUE OCT 12 1976'. Lore only.
Full jerry can: a silent inventory item from the kitchen, poured at blue hour. The empty RVX-318 can stays behind.

Ledger p1 (Harlan's room): 'Oct 14 '76. She came up out of the well. Did like Mother's book says: took the head, gave it back to the water. Holds her one night. / Nailed her room shut. She can't get past nails, just stands there scratching. I won't go in either.'

Ledger p2: 'She can't find me if she can't see me. Covered the glass. Cut myself out of the pictures. Sleep in the sack. She goes close to every face she finds, hunting mine. If she ever sees it she'll know me, and that's the end of me. Only picture left went down the well with her, in her locket.'

Ledger p3: 'Every pull in the house rings in the parlor now. She always comes to the bell. Always did. / She can't hear a thing under thunder. / The drifter kept her quiet a month. Did the Pruitt boy myself; didn't hold her an hour. She has to take them herself. / She works the latches now. She learns.'

Ada's unsent letter (sewing basket): 'Ruthie, Tuesday, the 6:10 to Carvel. He found the tin, so the ticket's sewn in the hem of my wedding dress, with the locket. I can't wear his face anymore, but I won't leave it for him. He says he'll put me down the well first. Let him try. I'll be at the depot if I have to wa'

Guest book (hall table): a ledger headed GUESTS, with columns Date / Name / Vehicle. Eleven lines from 1977 to 1994, all ruled through, e.g. 'Nov 3 '77, drifter, on foot' and 'Jun 22 '79, D. Pruitt, '72 Dodge Dart'. The last line reads 'Oct 11 '94' with name and vehicle blank. In the sting that line reads HARLAN, ruled through, with a new blank line below.
Two photos with Harlan's face knifed out: the wedding portrait in the hall (bride veiled), and 'Stroud's Gas & Feed, 1970' on the landing. Documents can be re-read in a journal (Tab).
design.fail_and_checkpoints:
Death is quick and not gory: a 3 s cutaway (a wet hand over the lens, hair filling the frame, one eye glint, black, a bubbling drowning rush), then an instant reload. Only position is lost. Items, pried boards, opened doors, read documents and the can all persist, and key items can't be dropped.

Checkpoints:
- CP1: at the gate after C1
- CP2: the hall as she rises (C2 replays in 3 s)
- CP3: after the first hide
- CP4: taking the hammer or ledger
- CP5: after each pried board
- CP6: taking the locket (the dress visit replays)
- CP7: taking the can
- CP8: the finale

Grace: after a death she restarts at the anchor farthest from you, PATROL-only, with hearing -30% for 20 s, and the bell lure resets to 60 s. The first hide can't be failed.

Assists:
- After 2 deaths in a section: she is 15% slower, her LOOK wind-up grows to 1.6 s, and noise radii shrink 20%.
- After 3: a shutter bangs far away to draw her off, or thunder comes on cue.
- After 2 failed pries: longer rumbles.
- Finale: running isn't an instant fail. After one finale death the scene restarts with the locket raised and a one-time prompt; after two, she waits at 4 m.

If you are stuck for 90 s, lightning picks out the next interactable. Cutscenes can be skipped after the first viewing. The game pauses when pointer lock is lost.

ending.name: The Keeping
ending.description: The only ending, earned by the escape theorem. Ada sees Harlan's face in your light and takes back her locket. In shadow on the tally wall, she ends the man who has ended her every night for eighteen years. Then she pulls his rope: he opened the door to bring you in, and she opens it to let you go. Blue hour, dripping eaves, mist over the dead cars. A dead guest's gasoline goes into your tank, the engine catches, the ROOMS lantern gutters out, and the house sinks into the mirror: real release after twelve minutes of dread. Then the sting reframes it: you freed her from her keeper, not from the house.
ending.final_sting: Weeks later, in rain, a different dashboard, fuel lamp blinking. The ROOMS lantern is lit again. A knock; the bell rings off to the right; the door opens by itself. The line that waited for your name reads HARLAN in wet capitals, ruled through, with a blank line under it. From the opening's exact threshold and lens: candlelight, the tally wall, and Ada in his rocking chair with a round, heavy sack tied at the neck in her lap. The rocking stops. She lifts her own head in one hand; with the other she raises the sack by its knot and turns its eyeholes to the doorway, as he once turned hers. Both of them look at you. Smash to black. One bell. THE KEEPING.

[M1] EXT2 Drive, yard, porch: facade and porch only. [M2] east-field wreck row (lightning and mist vista)
[M1] G1 Hall and main stair. [M2] back passage and under-stair closet
[M1] G2 Parlor: dressed for 3 fixed views plus the shadow wall; never free-roamed
[M2] G3 Kitchen and back passage
[M1] U1 Upper hallway and landing
[M1 greybox, M2 final] U2 Harlan's bedroom
[M2] U3 Ada's sewing room
[M2] U4 Servants' back stair
