The finale asks the player to stand still and let her look, which fights ten minutes of conditioning. Mitigation: the diary and letter make the logic explicit; a one-time contextual 'raise the locket' prompt appears once she is in view; Harlan's bell goes frantic; she approaches more slowly; the scene restarts forgivingly.

Players may miss the twist if they skip documents. Mitigation: every document is 60 words or fewer with one key line, and the twist can also be read without text: the field of cars, your plate on an empty can, the padlock on the outside of the hatch, the sack, the knifed photos.

The thunder-masking and bell-lure rules may go unnoticed. Mitigation: demonstrate each once before it is required (thunder swallowing her steps in B06; the doorbell ringing in the parlor in B02), keep the storm rhythm regular, and add assists after failures.

The sting's logic (she learns and keeps the house) could feel arbitrary. Mitigation: seed 'She works the latches now' in the diary, let her visibly open doors all game, and show 'HARLAN' ruled through in the guest book.
Moral weight: the player sends a man to his death. His crimes (guest book, cars, your plate) frame it, and the sting pays it off so the cost registers without glorifying it.

Browser performance with rain, fog, film post-processing and a shadowed flashlight. Mitigation: one shadow-casting spot (the flashlight), baked lightmaps per room, lightning as a global exposure/probe pulse, candles as non-shadowing flickering lights, room-portal culling, low-detail field cars.
Synthesized audio carries the AI tells (drip, drip stopping, crack, gurgle, bell). If these sounds aren't convincing, the rules aren't readable. Prototype this set in M1, before art polish.
AI fairness in a small house: tune noise radii per room, never relocate her in view, guarantee escape loops (hallway ↔ bedroom, kitchen ↔ hall), and cap how often she checks hides.
Scope: 10 spaces is the cap. If M2 slips, reduce the bathroom to a patrol alcove and make the sting's pickup a recoloured sedan interior.
Photosensitivity: lightning flashes are frequent. Provide a reduced-flash option, keep flashes below 3 Hz, and show a content warning (domestic violence, murder, drowning).
Browser input and audio: the audio context and pointer lock need a user gesture, so fold the first click into 'turn the ignition key' on the title screen, and pause when pointer lock is lost.

M3 polish debt is concentrated in a few places: Ada's LOOK and stutter animation, the drip, crack and gurgle sound design, lightning and baked lighting, per-room AI tuning, and hint timing. Protect time for these above new content.

designs.title: BEHELD
designs.logline: You run out of fuel at 3 a.m. and ring the bell of the only house for miles. The door opens by itself, and in the first room on the right a man in a burlap mask is beheading a woman. Both of them turn to look at you. Now she has seen your face, and she will not stop.
designs.lore: 1931: Maren Voss, housekeeper-maid at Harrow House, answered every bell on the kitchen bell board and carried the house keys on a chatelaine. Her master, Aldous Harrow, beheaded her in the parlor with a hay knife. He wore a feed sack over his head so she would never see who did it. She came back. The dead repeat themselves: she still answers bells (board first, then the room that rang), she kneels for a sack at the block, and she hunts the last face she saw, looking for her killer. Each night a Keeper performs the 'keeping': ring the bell, put out the light, wear the sack, wait at the block, take the head, lock it in the iron box. Then she sleeps until the next night, but only while her Keeper stays near. THE MAN is Daniel Kessler, a traveler stranded here in October 1989. She saw his face on his first night, and he has kept her every night for 37 years, masked. TWIST 1 (mid-game, deducible): he let you in. The door 'opened by itself' because he pulled the parlor's brass FRONT DOOR release. He stopped the cut halfway on purpose so that she would see YOUR face. Once she did, he was free: he rang the bell to pull her off you, drove away in his truck, and locked the house behind him. TWIST 2 (the sting): keeping her only holds her while her Keeper stays close. She comes back to the last face she saw. You are the new Keeper.

characters.name: The Traveler (player)
characters.role: Protagonist. Unnamed and never seen except for gloved first-person hands.
characters.appearance: Gloved hands, a wet jacket sleeve, a cheap flashlight. The face is never shown; the only mirror appears in the sting and shows the back seat.
characters.behavior: Walk, crouch and sprint; drag doors slowly or quickly; throw bottles; pull bells; hide in wardrobes or under beds; hold breath (covers mouth with a hand); read notes; carry the jerrycan (no sprint).

characters.name: Maren Voss, 'the Housekeeper' (the woman)
characters.role: The single active chaser. A 1931 revenant who is bound to the last face she saw.
characters.appearance: Long, wet black hair over the face, with one eye glimpsed. Grey waterlogged skin, a sodden black maid's dress, a stained apron, bare feet, and an iron chatelaine key ring at the hip. After the opening her neck is half-severed: the head hangs forward or lolls sideways, and she lifts it by the hair to see.
characters.behavior: Stop-motion movement (animation quantized to about 8–12 fps, with random skipped frames). Stutter-walks, then lunges. Answers bells. Kneels at the block when idle. To check under beds she bends over and her head flops upside down. She makes no voice sounds, only a wet whistle through the cut throat.

characters.name: Daniel Kessler, 'the Keeper' (the man)
characters.role: Scripted presence only: the opening scene, an off-screen bell pull, departing headlights, then the ledger and notes. Subtitles only, no speech.
characters.appearance: A burlap sack mask with ragged eyeholes and twine at the neck, an oilskin coat, heavy boots, a stoop. Seen only in firelight and shadow.
characters.behavior: In the opening he is mid-stroke and turns to look. Then he stops, as he planned. During the first hide he rings the parlor bell and escapes in his pickup, leaving the key ring 'for the next one'.

characters.name: Aldous Harrow
characters.role: Lore only: the original killer. Appears in the portrait and photos.
characters.appearance: Face scratched out in the landing portrait. In the staff photo he is a sack-headed silhouette.

house_layout.name: The Road
house_layout.description: Wet county road in fog. The car dies at the foot of the drive; the house sits on a rise 60 m up. Used again in the ending drive.

house_layout.name: Yard & Porch
house_layout.description: Gravel drive with mud ruts and a dead oak. Ground-floor windows are boarded. The slanted cellar bulkhead on the east wall is the final exit. Candle glow shows through the parlor shutters.

house_layout.name: Entrance Hall
house_layout.description: The staircase along the left wall rises to the landing. The first door on the right is the parlor; a back corridor leads to the kitchen. The front door has a double-keyed lock and locks after the opening scene.

house_layout.name: The Parlor (first room on the right)
house_layout.description: Scene of the opening and the finale. Her home spot: she kneels at the block when idle. A service door to the kitchen forms the ground-floor loop.
key_contents: oak chopping block on a drop cloth
hay knife stuck in the block
key ring on a hook, tagged 'for the next one'
iron keeping box on the sideboard
worn Keeper's mark on the boards

house_layout.name: Kitchen & Bell Board
house_layout.description: The hub of her routines: every bell sends her here first. Holds the throwables and the padlocked cellar door. The back door is nailed shut.
key_contents: bell board (FRONT DOOR, PARLOUR, BLUE ROOM, MAID, MASTER)

house_layout.name: Cellar
house_layout.description: Needed by the route: the only fuel, the Keeper's sack and the only unlockable exit are all here. Pitch black, so the flashlight is required. Standing water makes footsteps louder.
key_contents: workbench with a fresh sack tagged 'for the next one'
the '91 note nailed to a beam

house_layout.name: Landing
house_layout.description: A balustrade gallery around the stairwell with a tall end window for lightning. Warped, darker planks mark the creaky boards. The top of the stairs is her vigil point.

house_layout.name: The Blue Room (Keeper's room)
house_layout.description: 37 years of the Keeper's life. Site of the first hide and of the rules. Its window overlooks the yard.
key_contents: desk with the ledger and an oil lamp
five sacks on hooks, sixth hook empty

house_layout.name: The Maid's Room (optional)
house_layout.description: Optional lore detour. Maren's room, preserved since 1931. Offers a second bell lure and a bed hide.

beats.title: Empty
beats.description: Cutscene inside the car: wipers, rain, radio static, the fuel light blinking. The engine sputters and dies. Lightning shows the house on the rise. The player takes the flashlight from the glovebox.
beats.player_goal: None (cutscene)
beats.setpiece: The needle settles on E as a lightning flash lights up the house.

beats.title: The Walk Up
beats.description: Player control starts. The flashlight teaches itself through the darkness. Pass the Keeper's pickup (engine still ticking, a sack on the seat). Knock three times: nothing. Pull the bell: a bell sounds deep inside, the latch clicks, and the door swings open by itself.
beats.player_goal: Reach the house and ask for shelter
beats.setpiece: The door opens by itself onto darkness and the first sounds of chopping.

beats.title: The First Room on the Right
beats.description: A forced slow walk to the lit doorway on the right. At the threshold the controls lock. Cutaway gore only: the stroke appears as a shadow on the wall, followed by a wet thunk and spatter on the lampshade. The man and the woman both turn to look. She lifts her half-severed head by the hair and one eye shows, then she rises in broken frames.
beats.player_goal: Witness (controls locked)
beats.setpiece: Both heads turn: the sack mask and the one wet eye.

beats.title: Up
beats.description: The front door slams and locks, and the kitchen corridor door is shut, so the stairs are the only way. She follows in lunges at a scripted, uncatchable pace. Lightning through the landing window shows the open door of the Blue Room.
beats.player_goal: Run upstairs and hide
beats.setpiece: Her key ring jingling up the stairs behind you.

beats.title: The Wardrobe
beats.description: First-hide tutorial with a breath-hold prompt; this hide is scripted to be safe. She searches the room, checks under the bed with her head flopped upside down, then lifts her head at the slats. Downstairs a bell rings on the board, and she leaves: board, then parlor. An engine starts, headlights sweep across the slats, and the sound fades away. M1 ends here.
beats.player_goal: Hide and survive the search
beats.setpiece: Her eye an inch from the slats, then the bell rings below.

beats.title: The Ledger
beats.description: Required pickup: the ledger, which states the rules and 'the order of it'. Its final page reads 'she keeps to the last face she beheld … tonight I'll let the door open'. The empty sixth hook, the Polaroids, and the window showing the truck gone. Her throat-whistle comes from the top of the stairs.
beats.player_goal: Learn her rules and find a way down
beats.setpiece: The headlight ruts in the mud reveal the man abandoned you.

beats.title: Vigil
beats.description: Puzzle P1: she is kneeling at the top of the stairs, listening. Lure her away with a bell or a bottle, then time the descent.
beats.player_goal: Get downstairs unheard
beats.setpiece: She passes the player on the stairs in the dark, climbing back up to answer the bell.

beats.title: For the Next One
beats.description: Puzzle P2: take the key ring from the hook two paces behind her while she kneels at the block. The FRONT DOOR pull hanging beside it confirms the man let you in.
beats.player_goal: Take the key ring
beats.setpiece: Lifting the keys off the hook while she breathes wetly below them.

beats.title: Below
beats.description: Puzzle P3: unlock the cellar, fill the can and take the fresh sack. Unchain the bulkhead and lift the door: in lightning she is standing on the steps. The door slams, she pounds on it, then silence. Her keys jingle on the cellar stairs behind you, so hide in the coal bin. The '91 note reads 'KEEP HER, THEN GO'.
beats.player_goal: Get fuel and an exit, and learn why you can't leave yet
beats.setpiece: She is outside the bulkhead, then inside the house seconds later.

beats.title: The Keeping
beats.description: Puzzle P4: perform the ritual, re-enacting the opening from the man's side. The view is narrowed and the audio muffled by the sack. She kneels, and one hay-knife stroke is shown only as a cutaway: the shadow on the wall, the fire flaring, a sound. The head goes into the box in a cutaway, then the lid and the lock. The house goes quiet.
beats.player_goal: Keep her
beats.setpiece: She lifts her head, looks at the sack, and lays her own neck on the block.

beats.title: The Last Face
beats.description: Out through the bulkhead with the can. Refuel (hold to pour). The ignition fails once, then catches. An on-rails drive with free look: the rain thins, dawn comes, the radio finds a song, and the rearview mirror is empty. Then the sting.
beats.player_goal: Drive away
beats.setpiece: Three knocks from the back seat.

states: SCRIPTED: cutscene puppet
VIGIL: anchored at the parlor block (home) or the top of the stairs; head down; listening
PATROL: walks the authored room/door node graph at 1.1 m/s; 3 s listen-stop at each doorway
ANSWER: a bell rang; walk to the kitchen board, 'read' it for 6 s (head lifted, facing the board), then go to the room that rang and search it for 8 s
INVESTIGATE: move to the stimulus at 1.6 m/s; 8 s local search; one BEHOLD
BEHOLD: 0.8 s wind-up (stops, raises her hand, neck crackles, lifts head by the hair), then a 2 s sight scan
CHASE: lunge bursts toward the player's live position
SEARCH: 10 s at the last known position; BEHOLD every 3 s; checks a hide only if she has cause
CATCH: 1.5 s kill cinematic
KNEEL: finale only; sees the sack at the block in darkness
KEPT: headless and inert
chaser_ai.senses: HEARING (primary). Noise radius at the source; each wall or floor between halves it (counted on the room graph, no raycasts). Sprint 14 m, walk 6 m, crouch 2 m. Puddle splash 8 m, creaky plank 8 m. Door: slow drag 3 m, fast 10 m, slam 16 m. Bottle shatter 18 m at the impact point. Gasp 6 m. Panting (breath below 30) 3 m, or 2 m while hidden. Filling the can 5 m. LIGHT: the flashlight beam touching her within 12 m, or a lit flashlight within 6 m of her in any direction, triggers an immediate INVESTIGATE at the player's position plus a BEHOLD on arrival. The cupped beam only registers within 2 m. SIGHT: only during BEHOLD. 60-degree cone. Range 10 m if the player is unlit, 16 m if lit. Crouched in darkness beyond 4 m, or hidden, means not seen. The sack blocks sight-recognition only in the finale. TOUCH: within 0.8 m, CATCH.
chaser_ai.rules: Priority: CATCH > CHASE > ANSWER > INVESTIGATE(light) > INVESTIGATE(sound) > SEARCH > PATROL > VIGIL. Bells are ignored during CHASE, and each bell pull has a 30 s cooldown (the spring bell visibly quivers until it resets). CHASE speed: lunges of 4.5 m/s for 1 s every 3 s, averaging 3.4 m/s. Player sprint is 3.8 m/s but lasts at most about 6 s. She loses the player when line of sight has been broken for more than 4 s and no player noise over 3 m has occurred; she then switches to SEARCH. Hide rule (testable): a hide is safe unless she saw the player enter (line of sight in the last 2 s) OR the player is audible within 2 m of it. If she saw the entry, she checks that hide and CATCHes. She opens every door (1 s rip-open, since she holds the keys). She never checks a hide without cause, except for one scripted look in B05. The night escalates: after B08 her doorway stops shorten to 1.5 s, and after B09 she PATROLs rather than VIGILs.
chaser_ai.tells: Audio, all spatialized: a wet throat-whistle (10 m), the chatelaine jingle (its rhythm tracks her speed: slow clink, fast rattle, silence when she stops), bare-foot slaps, drips, and a sharp neck crackle that marks the BEHOLD wind-up. A dread drone swells with proximity. Visual: candle flames lean and gutter within 5 m of her; the flashlight stutters within 8 m; her one eye glints in the beam. BEHOLD is signposted: the jingle stops, her hand rises to the back of her head, the crackle sounds, and the head lifts. Checking under a bed: her head flops upside down into view.
chaser_ai.counterplay: Sound: crouch, drag doors slowly, avoid the warped planks and puddles, stay on rugs. Breath: sprint and breath-hold draw on one shared meter. Holding breath lasts up to 8 s from full; at 0 you gasp. Sprinting to a hide leaves little breath to hold, so break line of sight early. Light: switch the flashlight off, or cup it (hold RMB, 3 m reach), and never let the beam touch her. Sight: when you hear the crackle, get out of her cone, crouch in darkness, or close a door between you. Distraction: a bottle pulls her to its impact point; a bell pull sends her board-then-room, giving a predictable timed window. Hides: wardrobes, under beds and the coal bin, with a peek view; they are safe if you entered unseen and stay quiet. Doors: closing one cuts sight and halves sound, and her 1 s rip-open breaks the chase rhythm. Loop: hall, parlor and kitchen form a circuit for breaking line of sight.

obstacles_and_puzzles.name: P1 Vigil on the Landing
obstacles_and_puzzles.solution: Pull the BLUE ROOM or MAID bell, then hide or wait. She goes down to the kitchen board, reads it for 6 s, then comes back up to the room that rang. Descend while she is at the board, and duck into the parlor or under the stairs as she climbs back. Alternative: throw a bottle down the stairwell into the hall and slip past while she investigates.
obstacles_and_puzzles.clues: The bell lesson in B05 (a bell rang, she went board then parlor). Ledger: 'She answers the bells same as alive. Board first, then the room that rang.' Brass labels on each bell pull.

obstacles_and_puzzles.name: P2 Keys for the Next One
obstacles_and_puzzles.solution: Two options. (a) Flashlight off, crouch along the rug avoiding the warped planks, and lift the ring from the hook behind her while her head hangs, keeping out of her cone if she does a BEHOLD. (b) Pull the PARLOUR bell, wait out of sight, and take the ring while she is at the board, then leave through the kitchen loop before she returns.
obstacles_and_puzzles.clues: The key ring on the hook is visible in the B03 opening scene. Ledger: 'Head down she's blind as stone. She hears everything. She feels a lamp like heat.' The tag 'for the next one'. The worn Keeper's mark shows where the rug is quiet.

obstacles_and_puzzles.name: P3 Fuel in the Dark
obstacles_and_puzzles.solution: Unlock the cellar with the ring. The flashlight is needed down here, so use the cupped beam near her. Hold on the generator petcock for 8 s (a 5 m glug that can be paused, with progress kept) to fill the can. Take the fresh sack from the bench. Unchain the bulkhead; the scripted scare follows. Hide in the coal bin until she leaves. The bulkhead then stays barred ('She's out there.') until she has been kept.
obstacles_and_puzzles.clues: Ledger: 'Can's by the genny, tank's full.' The chain and padlock match the ring. The '91 note: 'Tried the road in '91. She was standing on it. You don't leave her walking. KEEP HER, THEN GO.'

obstacles_and_puzzles.name: P4 The Keeping
obstacles_and_puzzles.solution: Perform the steps in order: pull the PARLOUR bell; turn the flashlight off; put the sack on; stand on the worn mark behind the block; stay still and silent. She comes (board, then parlor), lifts her head, sees the sack and kneels. Hold LMB to pull the hay knife and strike (cutaway). Put the head in the iron box (cutaway), close the lid and lock it with the ring. Failures: light on, noise, standing off the mark, or no sack each lead to CHASE, with a retry from CP5.
obstacles_and_puzzles.clues: The opening scene: she knelt calmly for the masked man in firelight. Ledger: 'Nightly. Bell, sack, dark, block, knife, box. Lamp out or she won't kneel.' Polaroids of a masked Keeper beside her kneeling form. 'KEEP' scratched into the lid of the box.

designs.escape_theorem:
GOAL: drive away.
← The car needs fuel (clue: the B01 fuel gauge on E).
← Fuel is in the cellar generator's tank, drawn into the can (clue: ledger 'can's by the genny').
← The cellar is padlocked and the key ring hangs by the block (clues: seen in the opening; tag 'for the next one').
← She rests at the block, is blind while her head hangs, hears everything, feels light, and answers bells board-first (clues: B05 bell lesson; ledger pages; observed tells).
← The front door is locked and the man has the key; the only exit is the cellar bulkhead (clues: slammed front door; ring fits the bulkhead chain).
← You cannot leave while she walks, because she will be standing outside (clues: B09 non-lethal bulkhead scare, a mandatory demonstration; '91 note; the bulkhead stays barred with 'She's out there.').
⇒ She must be KEPT.
← She kneels only for the sack, in darkness, at the block, when called by a bell (clues: the opening scene; ledger 'Bell, sack, dark, block, knife, box'; Polaroids; the fresh sack on the cellar bench).
← Head in the iron box, locked ⇒ she sleeps ⇒ bulkhead ⇒ car.
HIDDEN CLAUSE (the sting): she sleeps only while her Keeper stays near, and she returns to the last face she saw. Mandatory clues: the ledger's final page in B06 ('she keeps to the last face she beheld') and the FRONT DOOR pull in B08. Attentive players feel dread; others get a fair shock.
items: Flashlight: from the glovebox; toggle F; hold RMB to cup the beam; stutters near her
Glass bottle or jar: carry 1; thrown lure
Key ring 'for the next one': opens the cellar padlock, the bulkhead chain and the keeping box
Jerrycan (5 gal): filled at the generator; blocks sprinting; clanks when you move fast
Burlap sack: the Keeper's mask; worn at the block (narrow view, muffled audio)
Hay knife: stuck in the block; used only in the keeping
Ledger and notes: auto-journal (J) holding the rules
designs.fail_and_checkpoints: Catch sequence: 1.5 s cinematic (hand over the lens, a curtain of hair, the one eye), then a 2 s fade and a reload. There are no lives. Items and solved steps persist. After a reload she starts at the anchor farthest from the player, with a 20 s grace period (PATROL only, hearing -30%). Autosave checkpoints: CP0 at the porch after B01; CP1 at the end of the B05 hide; CP2 at the foot of the stairs after P1; CP3 on taking the key ring; CP4 once the can is full; CP5 at the start of the ritual (sack in hand, in the parlor); CP6 after the keeping (no threat from then on). Adaptive assist per segment: after 2 deaths her hearing radii drop by 20% and her BEHOLD shortens by 25%; after 3 deaths a diegetic hint appears (the relevant ledger line glows in the journal, or lightning lights the route). Any partial can-fill progress is kept.

ending.name: The Last Face
ending.description: The player drives away with the can emptied into the tank. Dawn breaks, the radio plays a song, and the rearview mirror shows an empty back seat, so the player believes they have escaped. But the keeping only holds while its Keeper stays near, and she returns to the last face she saw. The man freed himself by giving her yours. You are the new Keeper, and she has come with you.
ending.final_sting: Three slow knocks from behind the driver's seat. In the rearview mirror a pale hand lifts her lolling head by its wet hair and one eye opens on you. Hard cut to black, and over the black a single servant's bell rings once.

risks: The woman's rig, strand-card wet hair and head-loll physics are the weakest area of realism. Mitigate with frame quantization, darkness, and short glimpses.
Readability in darkness: players may miss visual tells. Lean on the audio tells and the candle and flashlight cues, and playtest.
Players may not deduce the finale steps (light off, the mark). Keep the ledger line and Polaroids on the mandatory path, and use the adaptive hints.
Baked GI plus dynamic lights is costly in three.js. Limit shadow casters to the flashlight, fire and lightning, compress lightmaps with KTX2, and offer quality tiers.
Fog, volumetrics and film post-processing on weak GPUs need fake light cones and scalable passes.
The rearview-mirror reflection in the sting needs a render target. Enable it for the ending only.
AI stuck on stairs or doors: use an authored node graph with scripted door and stair traversal rather than a navmesh.
Soft-locks from lost or dropped key items: key items cannot be dropped, and checkpoint state must persist.
Browser pointer lock and audio unlock: gate the start on a click and resume the AudioContext then.
Beheading content and tone: keep every act as a cutaway, and offer a gore toggle as an option.
Scope creep in the parametric props and notes: freeze the props list at M1.

designs.title: HEADLIGHTS
designs.logline: Your car runs out of gas at three in the morning. You ring the bell of the only house for miles and walk in on a hooded man beheading a woman. She sits up and hunts you through the house. Learn her rules, restart the clock that controls her, and finish his stroke before the last chime. Then the door will open and your car will be ready. Nobody tells you who she follows home.
designs.lore:
Harrow House is a roadside inn from the early 1900s. It stands on a county road that nobody uses since the interstate opened. The sign at the gate still reads HARROW HOUSE — ROOMS, with a tin VACANCY plate hanging under it. Setting: one stormy night in October 1998 (analog dashboard, no phones).

THE WOMAN: Ada Harrow, the innkeeper's wife, drowned in her bath at 3:00 a.m. in 1931. The inquest called it an accident. Her husband Silas stopped the hall clock at the hour of her death, as mourners did, and that bound her to it. The next night she rose: wet, cold, and hunting anyone under her roof. Silas learned how the house works:
- When she walks, she stops the clock and drops its winding crank into her bath.
- If the clock is wound and made to strike three, she must go back to the parlor table where she was laid out and lie still until the last chime.
- If someone takes her head during those chimes, she stays down for the rest of the night.
Silas wore a feed sack so she would not see his face while he did it, and every Keeper since has worn one. She is not the victim of the scene the player walks in on; she is its monster. She was the victim 67 years ago.

THE MAN: Ray Dillard. He is not her husband and not a murderer. He is a stranded traveller exactly like you. He ran out of gas on this road on 12 Oct 1979, rang the bell at three, and walked in on the previous Keeper, Walter Pruitt (1958–79), beheading her. Ray has put her down every night since, about 6,900 nights, scratched as tally marks on his walls.

THE RULE NOBODY SAYS OUT LOUD: whoever takes her head becomes her Keeper. She never harms her Keeper, but she follows him out of the house and down any road. She only lies still while he sleeps under her roof. The only way out for a Keeper is for a new guest to finish the stroke.

So when your bell rang at three, Ray looked up at you and let the last chime pass with the stroke half done. He did it on purpose. His help afterwards is both real guilt and his way out: he rings the doorbell to pull her away from you, fills your tank from a can he kept 'for whoever comes next', and leaves a note telling you exactly what to do. The guestbook by the door records the chain, every entry in the same looping hand (Ada's; the house signs in its own guests). Each Keeper 'checks out' at 3:00 on the night the next guest 'checks in'.

THE TWIST: the escape plan is true. The door opens, the car runs, and you drive past Ray walking free. But you took her head, so you are the Keeper now, and she is in your back seat.

characters.name: S. Hale — the Driver (you)
characters.role: Player character: a first-person stranded traveller who becomes the next Keeper
characters.appearance: Never seen. The player only sees first-person hands and the cuffs of a waxed canvas jacket. The name appears only on the registration card clipped to the sun visor and, at the end, in the guestbook. Gender is left unspecified.
characters.behavior: Player-controlled and silent. Rare one-line thought subtitles appear only as hints when the player is stuck (e.g., after 90 s idle in the Keeper's room: 'The clock. It stopped when she passed it.'). One scripted thought in the opening cutscene sets up asking to stay the night.

characters.name: Ada Harrow — 'the Lady'
characters.role: The only AI chaser: a woman who drowned in 1931 and came back. She is the 'victim' in the opening scene who turns hunter.
characters.appearance: 1.65 m and gaunt. She wears a 1930s cotton nightdress, grey and see-through with water, clinging and dripping. Waist-length wet black hair always covers her face; the player only ever glimpses one clouded eye through a gap. Skin is grey-blue and blotchy, fingers long, nails dark, feet bare and leaving wet prints. After the opening scene her neck is half cut through: the head hangs on her left shoulder or swings behind her, and she must lift it upright with her own hand to see. Shading: wet look (dark base colour, strong highlights). Hair: clumped strips of hair texture with drip particles. The face is never modelled beyond a rough mask and one eye.
characters.behavior: She walks blind with her head hanging, listening. Her gait is jerky and puppet-like: a code-driven random twitch on the skeleton, which counts as a feature. Sound and light draw her. To see, she stops and holds her head up with one hand; this is the main warning sign, and only then can she see. She never harms her Keeper, never enters the Keeper's room, and never looks into her own bath. When the hall clock strikes three she drops everything, walks to the parlor table and lies down until the last chime. In the ending she rides in her new Keeper's back seat.

characters.name: Ray Dillard — 'the Keeper'
characters.role: Scripted presence only, never a chaser. He is the man in the burlap sack and the previous stranded traveller.
characters.appearance: 1.85 m, heavy-set, about sixty. Stained canvas work coat, a butcher's leather apron dark with old stains, rubber boots. A burlap feed-sack hood tied at the throat with twine; the two ragged eye holes show only black. He is only ever seen lit from behind by the parlor fire, as a lightning silhouette in the yard, or from behind in the car headlights on the road (hood off, grey hair flattened by rain). His face is never shown and never modelled.
characters.behavior:
He appears four times:
1. The opening scene: he strikes once, stops, turns his hood to you, drops the cleaver and backs out through the dark rear door.
2. Unseen, he rings the front doorbell to draw her away from your first hiding place.
3. In a lightning flash he stands by your car in the yard with a jerry can, looking up at your window.
4. In the ending he walks away up the road and does not turn as you pass.
His notes, his bell-pull board and your full fuel tank are both genuine help and his way out.

characters.name: Silas Harrow & Walter Pruitt (past Keepers)
characters.role: Background story only; never modelled as characters
characters.appearance: Silas appears only as a small suited figure in a 1928 wedding photo so water-damaged that both faces are lost. Pruitt exists only as a name and dates in the guestbook.
characters.behavior: They establish the chain the guestbook reveals: Silas (1931–58), then Pruitt (1958–79), then Ray (1979–tonight), then you.

house_layout.name: County road, gate & your car
house_layout.size_m: Road 7 m wide, about 60 m built (fog hides everything past about 25 m). The ending drive reuses it as a looping 400 m path through the fog.
house_layout.description: Two-lane county road in heavy rain: wet asphalt with procedural puddles, a ditch, fence posts, fog cards. The car dies at the gate. The headlights pick out 'HARROW HOUSE — ROOMS' and a swinging tin 'VACANCY' plate. Lightning shows the house outline 40 m up the drive: gabled roof, one warm window on the ground floor (the parlor, right of the door) and a faint candle upstairs (the guest room). The car interior is a detailed set used twice (opening and ending): analog fuel needle, dashboard clock, rain-streaked windscreen with wipers, a rear-view mirror (live mirror view only in the ending), back seat. The player only ever looks forward through the windscreen or up the drive.
connections: EXT2 via the gate and gravel drive
key_contents: Player car (main detailed asset: exterior + interior)
Gate + HARROW HOUSE — ROOMS sign with swinging VACANCY plate
Registration card 'S. HALE' on the sun visor
Road map with a pen-drawn detour on the passenger seat
Ending: burlap hood on the passenger seat; Ada in the back seat (seen only in the mirror)

house_layout.name: Yard, drive & porch
house_layout.size_m: Yard about 30 × 20 m (only the drive is walkable); porch 10 × 2.5 m; front wall 12 m wide × 9 m to the roof ridge
house_layout.description: A 40 m walk up a muddy drive. A dead oak stands over a car-shaped mound under a rotting tarp: Ray's 1979 car, which is the player-car model reused with rust material and flat tyres. Only the front wall of the house is detailed; the sides and back fade into fog. The porch has warped boards, a mechanical twist doorbell and an iron knocker on a heavy four-panel door with a glass fanlight above it. Only lightning shows the whole house. In the ending the same yard shows your car at the gate with its interior light on, driver door open, fuel cap open and an empty jerry can on its side.
connections: G1 (front door: opens by itself, seals when she rises, opens again after the final ritual)
key_contents: Ending: car with interior light on, empty jerry can

house_layout.name: Entrance hall & main stair
house_layout.size_m: 4 × 8 m, 3.2 m ceiling; stair 1.1 m wide with a window on the halfway landing
house_layout.description: Dark except for firelight spilling from the parlor doorway on the right, which pulls the eye on entry. The grandfather clock stands at the foot of the stair on the left. It ticks loudly until she stops it; after that its three weights hang at the bottom. A lectern by the door holds the guestbook. The stair rises along the left wall to a halfway landing with a tall window; lightning through it lights the escape route in the chase. The second door on the right (dining room) and the back door (kitchen) are barred from the far side; they are decorative dead ends. There is a closet under the stair (hiding spot). The player visits twice: entry, the opening scene and the chase in M1, then the clock-winding finale in M2, lit by the player's oil lamp.
key_contents: Grandfather clock (main prop: winding holes, glass face door, hands, pendulum, three weights)
Barred back door and dining-room door

house_layout.name: The Parlor (first room on the right)
house_layout.description: The room of the opening scene, composed for one fixed camera. The player stands on the threshold (west) and the fireplace is on the far (east) wall, so the man is always lit from behind. Between them is the long oak table where Ada lies, her head hanging off the near edge toward the player and her hair pooled on the floor. Candles stand on the mantel and table, and a fringed floor lamp by the door catches the blood spatter. Ray backs out through a dark rear doorway (north), which is barred from the other side afterwards. In the finale the fire is down to embers, the spatter is dry, and the cleaver still lies where he dropped it.
connections: Rear door (barred from the far side; set dressing only)
key_contents: Fringed floor lamp with spatter decal

house_layout.name: Upstairs hall & landing
house_layout.size_m: 12 × 1.8 m, 2.9 m ceiling; landing 2.5 × 2.5 m near the middle, toward the west
house_layout.description: A long corridor with a runner rug. The stair arrives at the landing just west of centre. At the west end are the Lady's bath and a tall sash window; lightning shows her silhouette at the end of the hall. At the east end is the guest room. Between them is the Keeper's door, nailed shut with planks; shadows can be seen through the gaps. Every door carries a brass shop bell on a coiled spring that jingles whenever the door moves. This is Ray's early-warning system and her easiest warning sign to read. The hall also has a linen cupboard (hiding spot) and a hall table with a flickering candle.
key_contents: Shop bells on springs on every door

house_layout.name: The Guest Room
house_layout.description: The only lit room when you reach the top of the stairs; a single candle glowing through the open door marks the way. It holds a turned-down bed (hide underneath and you only see her bare feet), a washstand with the candle, and a tall wardrobe with slatted doors (first hiding spot, with light shafts through the slats). The back panel of the wardrobe lets through a thin line of warm light: it is a false back into the Keeper's room. On the wall hangs the inn's printed 'Rules of the House' card, written over by generations of Keepers. The window looks over the yard and your car.
key_contents: Window over the yard (lightning shows Ray at your car)

house_layout.name: The Keeper's Room
house_layout.description: The safe room: she never comes in. The walls are scratched from floor to ceiling with about 6,900 tally marks, lit from the side by one desk candle. There is a cot, burlap hoods on nails, Ray's 1979 driver's licence (the photo bleached blank by sun) and a Polaroid of his new car at the gate, which is the wreck under the oak. The journal and a fresh note lie on the desk. A board of three bell-pull cords with enamel tags (BATH, GUEST, HALL) rings bells in those places. Through the gaps in the nailed door you can watch her shadow pass.
connections: U2 (wardrobe false back; the only way in or out)
key_contents: Drawer page (optional clue to the twist)

house_layout.name: The Lady's Bath
house_layout.description: Her lair: a claw-foot tub brim-full of black water inside a ring of candles, with wet footprints leading in from the hall. The vanity mirror is draped in black crepe, which is the mourning custom and also means no real-time mirror is needed. On the vanity are her hairbrush, clotted with black hair, the water-damaged wedding photo and the 1931 inquest newspaper clipping (optional story). On the windowsill are the Keeper's hurricane lamp and matches. The tub hides the crank, and later it hides you.
key_contents: Claw-foot tub + black water (crank; hide by going under)
Vanity: hairbrush, wedding photo, inquest clipping

beats.title: Running on Empty
beats.location: EXT1: car interior, county road, gate
beats.description: Opening cutscene, rendered in-engine from first person, about 60 s. Rain, wipers, fog. The dashboard clock reads 2:51. The fuel needle rests on E and the low-fuel light blinks. The map on the passenger seat has a pen-drawn detour, the radio is static, and the visor card reads 'S. HALE'. The headlights pick out a sign: HARROW HOUSE — ROOMS, with a tin VACANCY plate swinging. The needle sinks below E, the engine coughs and dies, and the car rolls to a stop at the gate. Lightning: a gabled house 40 m up the drive, one warm window on the ground floor, a faint candle upstairs. A subtitle thought (no voice): 'Nothing else for thirty miles. They'll have to let me stay the night.' Free look returns and the player gets out into the rain.
beats.player_goal: None during the cutscene; then open the door and step out.
beats.setpiece: Headlights through rain and fog, plus the first lightning flash showing the house. The needle sinking below E hints at something supernatural. Production: detailed car interior set + one strip of road + a flat outline of the house.

beats.title: The Bell
beats.description: A 40 m walk up a muddy drive; it is the only path, and fog blocks everything else. Lightning shows a dead oak over a car-shaped mound under a rotting tarp. The porch boards sag. Through the door you hear a big clock ticking. Knock: nothing but the tick. Twist the bell: a mechanical 'brrring', and inside, the clock begins its Westminster chime for three o'clock. The latch clicks and the door swings open by itself onto darkness, with a warm glow on the right.
beats.player_goal: Reach the front door; knock; ring the bell.
beats.setpiece: The door opens by itself on the first chime; the doorbell and clock sounds are timed together. Production: only the front of the house is built; the tarped wreck reuses the car model.

beats.title: Three O'Clock
beats.location: G1 hall to the G2 threshold
beats.description:
Inside: a dark hall, rain behind you, the clock on the left mid-chime, the stair rising on the left, and firelight spilling from the first doorway on the right. That glow is the only light. Reaching the threshold locks the view: the player freezes.
- Bong one: a man in a burlap sack, lit from behind by the fire, raises a cleaver over a woman laid on the table. Her head hangs upside down off the near edge, her wet black hair pooled on the floor.
- Bong two: the stroke. A lightning white-out cuts the frame and a single wet sound plays. After the flash, blood is spattered across the lampshade. He stops, and his hood turns toward you.
- Bong three: her upside-down head rotates on the half-cut neck, and one eye looks through the hair. Both of them are looking at you.
The last chime fades. She sits up and her head flops onto her shoulder. He drops the cleaver and backs into the dark rear doorway. The candles go out and she lurches toward you. Behind you, the front door slams shut by itself.
beats.player_goal: Watch (view locked); then run. The only open, lit route is the stair on the left.
beats.setpiece: The fire-lit scene with the stroke hidden by a lightning cut; gore is shown only as silhouette, sound and a spatter decal. Production: one fixed camera composition; neither face is ever lit.

beats.title: Upstairs
beats.location: G1 stair to U1 to U2
beats.description:
A scripted chase: she is held 3–5 m behind the player. As you reach the stair she swerves to the clock; her hand stops the pendulum and rips out the crank, and the ticking dies. A player who looks back sees her at the clock in a lightning flash. She climbs after you. At the top, one candle glows through an open door at the east end: the guest room. The wardrobe stands ajar. Hide. Through the slats:
- The door bell jingles and you hear dripping.
- She drifts to the candle, which flickers.
- Her hand lifts her head upright with a wet creak and she scans the room.
- As she nears the wardrobe, a prompt tells you to hold your breath.
Downstairs, the front doorbell rings: someone is outside. She lets her head fall and leaves. Seconds later comes a heavy splash from the far west end of the house. Checkpoint.
beats.player_goal: Outrun her up the stairs and hide without being found.
beats.setpiece: Hiding in the slatted wardrobe by candlelight. This scene shows every rule before any text explains it: light draws her, she lifts her head with her hand to look, bells and drips mark her movement, and sounds lure her away.

beats.title: Rules of the House
beats.description:
The inn's printed card on the wall begins 'Breakfast is served at seven…', but several Keepers have written over it by hand:
- 'Don't carry a light in the halls. She goes to light.'
- 'Walk soft. She hears everything.'
- 'If she lifts her head, DON'T MOVE.'
- 'If you hear the bells, she's moving. Stay put.'
- 'At three the clock calls her down.'
- In pencil: 'Hold your breath.'
Thunder draws you to the window. Lightning shows the hooded man in the yard beside your car, a jerry can in his hand, looking up at you; at the next flash he is gone. The hall is her territory and the Keeper's door is nailed shut, but a thin line of warm light glows at the back of the wardrobe. Push it and the back swings open.
beats.player_goal: Learn the rules; find the way forward (the wardrobe's false back).
beats.setpiece: Lightning shows the man at your car: a distant silhouette over two flashes.

beats.title: The Keeper's Room
beats.description:
A cell lit from the side by one desk candle, its light catching about 6,900 tally marks. Burlap hoods hang on nails. There is a cot, a 1979 licence, and a Polaroid of a new car at the gate: the wreck under the oak. The journal reads:
- 'Oct 12 1979. Ran dry on the county road. Rang the bell at three and the door opened by itself. A man in a feed sack was killing a woman on the parlor table. They both looked at me.'
- 'Ada Harrow drowned in her bath at three in the morning, 1931. The clock is the only thing she answers to.'
- 'When she gets up she stops the clock and drowns the crank in her bath. Fish it out. Wind all three weights. Set it to three. She HAS to lie down. You have until the last chime.'
- 'She never touches her Keeper. She never comes in here. Pull the cord for where you want her. If she comes, hide where she sleeps — she never looks there.'
A fresh note under the candle: 'If you're reading this, I stopped. I'm sorry. Wind the clock, set it to three, take her head before the last chime. The door will open. Your car will be ready. Go, and don't look back. — R.D.'
Optional drawer page: 'Drove to the county line in '81. She was in the back seat. Whoever takes her head, she follows.'
Dripping passes outside, and her shadow slides by the gaps in the planks.
beats.player_goal: Learn the escape plan; find the bell-pull board.
beats.setpiece: A breather in the safe room: side-lit candle on the tally wall, and her shadow passing the nailed door (a scare with no danger).

beats.title: The Black Bath
beats.location: U3 to U2 to U1 to U4
beats.description: Pull HALL: a bell rings above the front door. Dripping passes the nailed door and goes down the stair. Go out through the wardrobe and west along the hall past the landing into her bath: a claw-foot tub of black water in a ring of candles, the mirror draped in black crepe, wet footprints leading in. Search the water. The first handful comes up wrapped in long black hair; the second brings up the crank. The landing door bell jingles: she's back. Get into the tub and go under. Everything is black and muffled, with candle glow wavering overhead. She stands over you with her hair drifting down into the water above your face. The creak; she looks around the room, never into the tub, and leaves. You surface gasping, and your flashlight sputters orange and dies. Strike a match and light the Keeper's hurricane lamp from the windowsill.
beats.player_goal: Lure her away, get the crank, survive her return, and find a new light.
beats.setpiece: Hiding underwater beneath her, then the flashlight dies. For the rest of the game the light is warm, flickering oil light, which also draws her.

beats.title: Winding
beats.description: With the lamp wick turned low, go down the stair behind her back. The hall is now lit by your lamp and the parlor embers: the stopped clock (3:01, weights at the bottom of the case), the guestbook in the dark, and the front door that won't move. Open the case and fit the crank; every turn is a loud ratchet click. Dripping, the landing bell and creaking stairs mean she's coming. You can stop and slip into the closet under the stair. Or set the lit lamp down in the parlor doorway, let her go to it, and wind in the dark. The weights stay wound between attempts. Once all three weights are up, open the glass face and push the hands to three. The chime begins, and she stops wherever she is, even mid-lunge if she was charging. Her head drops and she walks past you into the parlor.
beats.player_goal: Wind all three weights and set the clock to three without getting caught.
beats.setpiece: A loud task under threat, managed with the lamp you can set down as a lure. When the clock strikes, the hunter turns away mid-lunge and brushes past you.

beats.title: The Last Chime
beats.description: Follow her in; now the hunted follows the hunter. She lies down on the table exactly as in the opening scene, head hanging off the near edge, hair pooled on the floor. The cleaver lies in the dark stain where it fell. Pick it up and stand where the man stood. Hold to raise it. Her eye opens through the hair, upside down, and looks at you. The third bong: white-out, black, one wet sound. Then the clock's tick resumes, and out in the hall the front door creaks open onto the rain.
beats.player_goal: Take her head before the last chime fades.
beats.setpiece: The opening scene repeated with you in the man's place. The gore stays entirely off-screen.

beats.title: Checking Out
beats.description: By the open door the guestbook lies open, every entry since 1931 in the same looping hand. The last two lines are wet: 'R. Dillard — in 12 Oct 1979 — out 3:00 a.m.' and below it 'S. Hale — in 3:00 a.m.' Outside, your car waits at the gate: interior light glowing through the rain, driver door open, fuel cap open, an empty jerry can on its side. On the passenger seat lies the wet burlap hood.
beats.player_goal: Leave the house; get into the car.
beats.setpiece: The car's interior light glowing in the rain, and three quiet clues to the twist: the guestbook, the jerry can and the hood.

beats.title: Headlights
beats.description: Turn the key: the engine catches and the needle climbs. The drive follows a fixed path; the player can look around, limited to ±70°. The headlights find a man walking up the road, hood gone, grey hair plastered down, his back to you. He steps onto the verge and does not turn as you pass. The radio drifts out of static into an old waltz. Then: dripping behind you. Lightning. The rear-view mirror.
beats.player_goal: Drive away.
beats.setpiece: The rear-view mirror sting is built from the two warning signs the player has learned to fear: dripping means she is near; the creak and the hand lifting her head mean she sees you.

states: DORMANT: lies on the parlor table (before the opening scene and after the final ritual).

SCRIPTED: driven by a timeline. Covers her rising in the opening scene, stopping the clock, the first chase (held 3–5 m behind the player), the first hiding sequence, leaning over the tub, the compelled walk and the back-seat sting.

ROAM: walks a hand-built patrol route at 0.9 m/s with her head hanging, which means she is blind. The route runs bath, landing, hall, guest room; in Act 3 it adds the stair, the ground-floor hall and the parlor. She pushes doors (so their bells jingle) and idles by the candles at her bath.
INVESTIGATE: when she hears a noise or notices light, she walks at 1.5 m/s to where it came from. She is still blind on the way.

LOOK: at the source of a noise or light, or every 20–30 s while roaming, she stops and lifts her head upright with her hand. This takes 0.8 s and plays the neck creak; she then scans for 2.5 s. She can only see during this state. If she sees you she switches to CHASE; if not, to SEARCH or ROAM.
CHASE: a lurching run at 3.0 m/s, holding her head up so she can keep seeing. She loses you after 3 s without line of sight while you are dark and quiet, and switches to SEARCH.
SEARCH: a 10 s sweep around where she last knew you were. She opens a hiding spot ONLY if she saw you get into it or hears you breathing within 1.5 m. Then she returns to ROAM.
GRAB: triggers within 1.1 m during CHASE, or if you walk into her. She lunges, hair fills the screen, one eye shows, and the screen cuts to black on the sound. The game reloads the last checkpoint.

COMPELLED: starts the moment the hall clock begins striking three and overrides every other state, even mid-lunge. Her head drops, she walks to the parlor table and lies there until 4 s after the last bong.
chaser_ai.senses:
SOUND (her main sense; always on). Every noise has a hearing radius:
- Crouch-walking 0.5 m; walking 3 m; sprinting 10 m.
- Moving a door (its bell rings) 6 m; slamming a door 15 m.
- Each click of the clock crank 12 m.
- A bell-board bell reaches her anywhere in the house and draws her to its room.
- Breathing while hiding without holding your breath 1.5 m (3 m after sprinting); a gasp when surfacing or when a held breath runs out 4 m.
A closed door halves the radius; the open stairwell cuts it to three-quarters. She goes to the loudest recent noise.

LIGHT (always on, even though she is blind):
- A flashlight beam touching her makes her LOOK toward it instantly.
- Your carried light within 8 m with line of sight makes her INVESTIGATE toward you.
- Any flame or lamp left unattended within 12 m draws her to it, and she LOOKs there. This is how the lure works.
- Candles flicker when she is within 4 m.

SIGHT (only while she LOOKs or CHASEs, i.e., while she holds her head up): a 50° cone. She sees you within 4 m if you are dark, 14 m if you carry a lit light, and 20 m if your beam is on her. Lightning never reveals you (for fairness).
chaser_ai.rules:
The rules are written on the guest-room card and then shown in play:
1. She is blind while her head hangs; she can only see when she holds it up.
2. She hears everything. Crouching is silent.
3. She goes to light, whether you carry it or leave it behind.
4. If you hear the door bells, she is moving.
5. She never enters the Keeper's room, never looks into her own bath, and never harms her Keeper.
6. When the clock strikes three she must go and lie on the parlor table until the last chime. Nothing overrides this.
7. She never appears or teleports where you can see. After a reload she restarts out of sight, roaming.
8. Only she can kill you; there are no other death traps.
chaser_ai.tells:
AUDIO:
- Dripping from her hair, placed in 3D space and audible within 12 m: she is near.
- Wet bare footsteps.
- The bell of any door she pushes.
- A wet rattle from the torn throat within 4 m.
- The neck creak (a wet, crackling sound): she will be able to see in 0.8 s.
- A gargled shriek, heavy footfalls and a clashing string sting: she is chasing you.

VISUAL:
- Silhouette with the head hanging on the shoulder: blind.
- Hand rising to the head: about to see.
- Candles and your lamp flame bend and flicker when she is within 4 m.
- Shining wet footprints (fading over 60 s) show where she has been.
- Water drips from the ceiling where she stood.
chaser_ai.counterplay:
- Crouch to move silently.
- When you hear dripping, switch off the flashlight or turn the lamp wick down.
- When her hand goes up, freeze in the dark or break line of sight. In the dark and more than 4 m away, you are invisible.
- Hide in the wardrobe, the linen cupboard, the closet under the stair, under the guest bed, or under the water in her bath. Hold your breath (Space, up to 9 s) when she is within about 2 m.
- Lure her with the Keeper's bell-pull board (BATH/GUEST/HALL), or set your lit lamp down somewhere else (G) and work in the dark.
- Never let her see you get into a hiding spot.
- You can outrun her briefly: you sprint at 4.0 m/s for 6 s against her 3.0 m/s, then you must hide.
- In the finale, make the clock strike three. It stops her in her tracks.

obstacles_and_puzzles.name: The Wardrobe's False Back
obstacles_and_puzzles.where: U2 Guest Room to U3 Keeper's Room
obstacles_and_puzzles.solution: Push the back panel of the wardrobe you hid in. It swings open into the Keeper's room, which is the only way in because his hall door is nailed shut.
obstacles_and_puzzles.clues: During the first hide, a thin line of warm light glows at the back of the wardrobe. The Keeper's door in the hall is planked shut, yet light shows under it. The wardrobe's back panel is visibly newer wood.

obstacles_and_puzzles.name: The Bell Board
obstacles_and_puzzles.where: U3 Keeper's Room (affects the whole upper floor)
obstacles_and_puzzles.solution: Pull HALL. A bell rings above the front door downstairs, she goes down to answer it, and the upper floor is clear for about 40 s, long enough to reach her bath. Pulling GUEST brings her into the next room; you wait safely until she wanders off. Pulling BATH rings where she already is and does nothing.
obstacles_and_puzzles.clues:
- The first hide taught it: the doorbell drew her away.
- Journal page 4: 'Pull the cord for where you want her.'
- Rules card: 'If you hear the bells, she's moving.'
- The cords have enamel labels.
- The splash from the west end tells you the bath is where you need to go.

obstacles_and_puzzles.name: The Black Bath
obstacles_and_puzzles.solution: Hold E to search the black water. The first handful brings up her hair; the second brings up the crank. When the landing door bell jingles, she is back: get into the tub and go under. Hold your breath while she stands over you, then surface after she leaves. Your flashlight dies from the water; light the Keeper's hurricane lamp from the windowsill.
obstacles_and_puzzles.clues:
- A heavy splash from the west end right after the first hide.
- Wet footprints leading into the bath.
- Journal page 3: 'she drowns the crank in her bath'.
- Journal page 4: 'hide where she sleeps — she never looks there'.
- The pencilled 'Hold your breath' on the Rules card.
- The tub shows the same hide prompt as the wardrobes.

obstacles_and_puzzles.name: The Stopped Clock
obstacles_and_puzzles.solution: Open the case, fit the crank and wind all three weights: 12 loud clicks in total, done in short bursts. When dripping and bells come close, stop and hide in the closet under the stair, or set the lit lamp down in the parlor doorway as a lure. The weights stay wound between attempts. Then open the glass face and set the hands to three. The Westminster chime starts and she is forced to go to the parlor.
obstacles_and_puzzles.clues:
- The ticking died the moment she passed the clock in the chase; players who look back see her hand stop the pendulum.
- The hands are frozen at 3:01.
- The weights hang at the bottom.
- Rules card: 'At three the clock calls her down.'
- Journal pages 2–3: 'Wind all three weights. Set it to three. She HAS to lie down.'

designs.escape_theorem:
GOAL: drive away.

1. Drive away ⇐ the front door is open ∧ the car has fuel.
2. Car has fuel ⇐ Ray fills it while you are upstairs. You see him by lightning from the guest-room window, and the empty jerry can confirms it. No player action is needed; the note promises 'your car will be ready'.
3. Front door open ⇐ she lies still. The door opened for a guest, slammed when she rose, and only opens when she is down (Rules card + journal).
4. She lies still ⇐ her head is taken while she lies on the parlor table, before the last chime. Evidence: the opening scene itself, and journal page 3 ('you have until the last chime'). This needs the cleaver, which lies on the parlor floor where Ray dropped it.
5. She lies on the table ⇐ the hall clock strikes three. Evidence: the Rules card, and journal page 2 (she drowned at 3 a.m., and the stopped clock is the only thing she answers to).
6. The clock strikes three ⇐ the clock is wound (all three weights) ∧ its hands are set to three. Evidence: the ticking stopped as she passed it, the weights sit at the bottom, and journal page 3.
7. Winding ⇐ the crank ⇐ the bottom of her bath. Evidence: the splash after the first hide, and journal page 3 ('she drowns the crank in her bath').
8. Reaching the bath alive ⇐ she is somewhere else ⇐ pulling the HALL bell cord ⇐ being in the Keeper's room ⇐ the wardrobe's false back ⇐ surviving the first chase by hiding in the lit guest room.
9. Surviving the bath ⇐ hiding where she never looks, the tub (journal page 4). The cost: the flashlight drowns, so the finale is played with the oil lamp, which also draws her.

HIDDEN RULE (the twist): whoever takes her head becomes her Keeper. She never harms the Keeper, but she follows him everywhere and lies still only while he stays under her roof. Clues: the optional drawer page ('county line… back seat'), the guestbook's chain of check-ins and check-outs in her hand, Ray walking free, and his hood on your passenger seat.

CONCLUSION: every step is valid and you really do escape the house, but following the plan to the end takes her out with you.
items: Car keys: you start with them; used in the ending to turn the ignition.
Flashlight: you start with it. Cold white beam with a lens-ring pattern; press F to toggle. It is the light that gives you away. It drowns and dies in the bath (B07).
Winding crank: fished out of the black water in her bath (B07); used to wind the hall clock (B08).

Hurricane oil lamp + matches: the Keeper's, found on the bath windowsill (B07). Warm light in every direction. The mouse wheel turns the wick up or down (brighter means she notices you from further away). Press G to set it down or pick it up; a lamp left somewhere works as a lure.
Cleaver: on the parlor floor where Ray dropped it (B09); used once, in the final ritual.

Documents, collected automatically into a notebook you can re-read, with subtitles:
- Rules of the House card (U2)
- Ray's journal pages 1–4 and his fresh note (U3)
- Optional: the drawer page (U3)
- Optional: Ray's licence and Polaroid (U3)
- Optional: the wedding photo and the 1931 inquest clipping (U4)
- The guestbook (G1, readable in B10)
Things you use in place but never carry: the bell-pull cords, the wardrobe's false back, the clock case, face and hands, the tub, the hiding spots, the jerry can and the burlap hood.
designs.fail_and_checkpoints:
The only way to die is for her to grab you. The screen cuts to black on the sound for 1.5 s, then the game reloads instantly (no loading screen) at the last checkpoint, with her restarted out of sight and roaming. Items and puzzle progress are kept: the clock weights stay wound and you keep the crank. There are no other death traps.

Checkpoints (saved automatically in the browser):
- CP0: in the car.
- CP1: on the porch, at the knock.
- CP2: at the foot of the stair after the opening scene. On a retry the scene is skipped and she comes out of the parlor.
- CP3: after the first hide (end of M1).
- CP4: on entering the Keeper's room (safe room).
- CP5: with the crank in hand, before going under the water.
- CP6: with the lamp lit, after the bath.
- CP7: at the clock; each wound weight is saved separately.
- CP8: once the chime has started.
- CP9: outside the front door.

Forgiveness rules:
- The scripted first chase cannot be lost unless the player stands still for more than 2 s, and on a retry she is 20% slower.
- In the tub, if you surface early or run out of breath while she is there, you reload at CP5, and she now leaves after 5 s instead of 7.
- The game quietly gets easier after repeated deaths. After 2 deaths in the same beat, her hearing radii drop 25%, her LOOK scan is 30% shorter and her chase speed drops 10%. After 4 deaths, she stays away an extra 45 s after the next lure, and you can hold your breath for 12 s instead of 9.
- In the final ritual, if the last chime fades before you strike, she rises; you retry from CP8 with the chime starting again.
- The game pauses automatically if the mouse lock is lost.
- Every cutscene can be skipped after the first viewing.

ending.name: Checked Out
ending.description: The cleaver falls on the third bong: white-out, black, one wet sound. Then the clock ticks again and the front door creaks open onto the rain. By the door the guestbook lies open, every entry in the same old looping hand, the ink still wet: 'R. Dillard — in 12 Oct 1979 — out 3:00 a.m.' and below it 'S. Hale — in 3:00 a.m.' Your car waits at the gate with its interior light on, fuel cap open and an empty jerry can on its side. Ray's wet burlap hood lies on the passenger seat. The engine catches and the needle climbs. Your headlights find Ray walking up the road, hood gone, his back to you. He steps onto the verge and does not turn as you pass. The radio drifts into an old waltz. For a few seconds it is over.
ending.final_sting: Dripping, from behind you. Lightning. In the rear-view mirror something sits in the back seat. A wet creak, the sound you learned means she can see you, and her hand lifts her own head into the mirror by its hair. One clouded eye opens and looks at you. Cut to black. Tick... tick... one deep bong. Title: HEADLIGHTS.

risks: Twist fairness. The explicit line 'she follows whoever takes her head' is on an optional page, so some players may feel cheated. Mitigation: three hints on the main route (the guestbook chain in B10, the hood on the passenger seat, Ray walking free), and the sting reuses the dripping and neck-creak sounds players already fear. If playtests show confusion, move the drawer line onto the back of Ray's fresh note.

Human realism is the weakest link. Mitigation:
- Ada's face is never modelled beyond one eye.
- She is always covered by hair, head hanging, lit from behind, seen through slats, under black water, from behind, or in a half-second mirror flash.
- Ray never shows a face.
- The camera never gets within 1 m of either character with light on them, except in the scripted final ritual (upside down, face covered by hair).
- Her gait is meant to be jerky, so animation errors read as intentional.

Long wet hair built from scratch. Strips of hair texture with simple physics can look plastic. Mitigation: heavy wet clumping, drip particles, darkness, and a lower-detail hair version at distance. Prototype it in the first two weeks of M1.

Photorealism and performance in the browser. Mitigation:
- Baked lighting: pre-computed lightmaps rendered in Blender for each room, with a normal-night and a lightning version blended during flashes.
- At most one live light casting shadows at a time (the flashlight or the lamp).
- Compressed textures generated by code.
- Only the current floor is drawn.
- Resolution drops automatically when needed.
- Target 60 fps on integrated GPUs at 900p–1080p.
- Shaders are warmed up in advance to avoid stutters at the first lightning flash or chase.

The lighting-bake pipeline is the critical path. Blender Python must automatically unwrap a second texture layout, bake the lightmaps and export every space. Build it in week 1 of M1, or the photoreal target falls apart.

Realism of synthesized audio. Rain, thunder and bells synthesize convincingly, but the shriek and throat rattle may sound electronic. Keep them short, low in the mix and covered by music stings. The dripping and neck-creak sounds must be instantly recognizable, because the ending sting depends on them.

No downloaded fonts. Handwriting and the printed Rules card need a single-stroke alphabet defined in code (letters drawn as lines, with slight wobble like ink) and rendered to an image. Menus and subtitles can use the system's serif fonts. Budget this work explicitly.

Difficulty spikes in the B04 chase and the B08 clock winding. Tune them using logged deaths per beat, keep winding progress between attempts, rely on the automatic easing after deaths, and hold her at a set distance during scripted chases.

Players may not understand the tub hide. They may not think to climb into her bath. Mitigation: the tub shows exactly the same hide prompt as other hiding spots, the journal line is on the main route, and she only returns after the crank is in hand.

Rear-view mirror sting. It needs a small live mirror image (512×256), used only in the ending. The back seat must not be visible directly (free look limited to ±70°), so the mirror carries the reveal. If the mirror is too costly, fake it with a pre-framed rendered image.

Photosensitivity and accessibility. Lightning white-outs and the cut in the final ritual can trigger seizures. Ship a reduced-flash mode (lower peak brightness, 150 ms fade-in) and a warning. Add subtitles and optional on-screen captions for all of Ada's warning sounds for deaf and hard-of-hearing players.
Browser quirks with mouse lock (Safari, ESC, losing focus). Pause automatically when the mouse lock is lost, show a resume prompt, and test on desktop Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari.
Tone: the player carries out the beheading. Present it as putting down a monster and keep it strictly off-screen (white-out, then black). Her eye opening is the only image that lingers.

Milestone gates:
- M1 (B01–B04 at final quality, about 4.5 min) is done when strangers can say 'dripping means she's near, hand to head means she sees you' after one play, and it runs at 60 fps.
- M2 (B05–B11: full AI, all interactions, the ending) is done when a first-time player finishes in 11–15 min without outside hints.
- M3 (baked lighting, colour grading, audio mix, AI tuning, performance, accessibility) changes no layout or script. Any new feature requested after M2 is cut.
